articles.summaryTr: Demokratların Kongre’de çoğunluğu elde etmesinin ekonomi politikaları ve piyasalar üzerine etkileri gündeme geldi. Yapay zeka veri merkezi yatırımlarındaki harcamaların yavaşlamasıyla enflasyon baskısının hafifleyebileceği, bunun da Fed’in faiz artırımı beklentilerini azaltabileceği öngörülüyor.
articles.articleText: Demokrat zaferi sonrası Fed'den makas değişikliği beklentisi: Tim Waterer değerlendirdi - ABD ara seçimlerinde Demokratların Senato ve Temsilciler Meclisi’nde çoğunluğu elde etmesinin ekonomi politikaları ve piyasalar üzerindeki olası etkileri gündeme geldi. - Yapay zeka veri merkezi yatırımlarındaki harcamaların yavaşlamasıyla enflasyon baskısının hafifleyebileceği, bunun da Fed’in faiz artırımı beklentilerini azaltabileceği öngörülüyor. Demokratların ABD ara seçimlerinde Senato ve Temsilciler Meclisi'nde çoğunluğu almasının, yapay zeka veri merkezi harcamalarını azaltıp enflasyon baskısını hafifletebileceği ve Fed'in faiz artırım beklentilerini etkileyebileceği öngörülüyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle ABD Kongresi ara seçimlerinde Demokratların, Senatonun ardından Temsilciler Meclisi'nde de çoğunluğu Cumhuriyetçilerden almasıyla yapay zeka veri merkezleri kaynaklı harcamaların azalabileceği ve bunun enflasyonist baskıları hafifleterek ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) faiz artırımı beklentilerini etkileyebileceği öngörülüyor. ABD Kongre ara seçimlerinde Demokratların çoğunluğu elde etmesiyle ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın ABD/İsrail-İran Savaşı konusunda daha ılımlı bir yaklaşım sergileyebileceğine yönelik umutlar arttı. Böyle bir gelişme olması halinde enerji maliyetlerinin ve küresel faiz oranlarına yönelik yukarı yönlü baskının azalabileceği öngörülüyor. Fed, Ortadoğu kaynaklı enerji arzına ilişkin endişelerin enflasyonist baskıları artırmasıyla eylülde, 2023 yılından bu yana ilk kez faiz artırımına giderek, politika faizini 25 baz puan artırıp yüzde 3,75-4 aralığına yükseltmişti. Teknoloji sektörüne dikkat çekti Avustralya merkezli KCM Trade Global Baş Piyasa Analisti Tim Waterer, Demokratların Kongre’de çoğunluğu ele geçirmesinin piyasa açısından teknoloji sektörü için yaşanabilecek en kötü senaryo olabileceğini belirtti. Yapay zeka veri merkezlerinin hızla yaygınlaşmasına yönelik muhalif duruşun bundan önce birçok Kongre seçim yarışında öne çıkan başlıca meselelerden biri olduğunu ifade eden Waterer, şu değerlendirmelerde bulundu: "Demokratlar, kampanya dönemindeki vaatlerini yerine getirirse, yapay zeka veri merkezi inşaatlarının hızında bir yavaşlama yaşanabilir. Bu durumun kendisi bile ABD ekonomisi üzerinde hafif bir dezenflasyonist etki yaratabilir. Bu da Fed'in bundan sonraki süreçte faiz artırımlarında ne kadar agresif davranması gerektiğine ilişkin beklentilerin bir miktar aşağı çekilmesine yol açabilir." Finansal hizmetler şirketi Capital.com'un Kıdemli Finansal Piyasalar Analisti Kyle Rodda ise "İlk bakışta piyasalar, bu gelişmeyi ABD’nin maliye politikası kaynaklı ekonomik teşvikinin zayıflayacağı şeklinde yorumluyor. Bunun temel nedeni, Kongre’nin Trump yönetiminin maliye politikalarını engellemesi veya sekteye uğratmasına dair beklentiler. Bu durum, ABD'de enflasyon ve faiz oranları üzerindeki yukarı yönlü riskleri bir miktar azaltıyor." ifadelerini kullandı.
articles.articleTextTr: Demokrat zaferi sonrası Fed'den makas değişikliği beklentisi: Tim Waterer değerlendirdi - ABD ara seçimlerinde Demokratların Senato ve Temsilciler Meclisi’nde çoğunluğu elde etmesinin ekonomi politikaları ve piyasalar üzerindeki olası etkileri gündeme geldi. - Yapay zeka veri merkezi yatırımlarındaki harcamaların yavaşlamasıyla enflasyon baskısının hafifleyebileceği, bunun da Fed’in faiz artırımı beklentilerini azaltabileceği öngörülüyor. Demokratların ABD ara seçimlerinde Senato ve Temsilciler Meclisi'nde çoğunluğu almasının, yapay zeka veri merkezi harcamalarını azaltıp enflasyon baskısını hafifletebileceği ve Fed'in faiz artırım beklentilerini etkileyebileceği öngörülüyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle ABD Kongresi ara seçimlerinde Demokratların, Senatonun ardından Temsilciler Meclisi'nde de çoğunluğu Cumhuriyetçilerden almasıyla yapay zeka veri merkezleri kaynaklı harcamaların azalabileceği ve bunun enflasyonist baskıları hafifleterek ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) faiz artırımı beklentilerini etkileyebileceği öngörülüyor. ABD Kongre ara seçimlerinde Demokratların çoğunluğu elde etmesiyle ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın ABD/İsrail-İran Savaşı konusunda daha ılımlı bir yaklaşım sergileyebileceğine yönelik umutlar arttı. Böyle bir gelişme olması halinde enerji maliyetlerinin ve küresel faiz oranlarına yönelik yukarı yönlü baskının azalabileceği öngörülüyor. Fed, Ortadoğu kaynaklı enerji arzına ilişkin endişelerin enflasyonist baskıları artırmasıyla eylülde, 2023 yılından bu yana ilk kez faiz artırımına giderek, politika faizini 25 baz puan artırıp yüzde 3,75-4 aralığına yükseltmişti. Teknoloji sektörüne dikkat çekti Avustralya merkezli KCM Trade Global Baş Piyasa Analisti Tim Waterer, Demokratların Kongre’de çoğunluğu ele geçirmesinin piyasa açısından teknoloji sektörü için yaşanabilecek en kötü senaryo olabileceğini belirtti. Bunun temel nedeni, Kongre’nin Trump yönetiminin maliye politikalarını engellemesi veya sekteye uğratmasına dair beklentiler. articles.articleText: Avrupa'da peş peşe bomba ihbarı alarmları! 10'dan fazla yolcu uçağı acil iniş yaptı - Avrupa'da Polonya, Belçika, Çekya, İtalya, Fransa, Avusturya ve Bulgaristan'ı kapsayan bomba ihbarları nedeniyle çok sayıda yolcu uçağı acil iniş yaptı veya güvenlik kontrolüne alındı. İhbarların koordineli ya da hibrit saldırı kapsamında olup olmadığı araştırılıyor. Avrupa'da İtalya, Fransa, Belçika, Çekya ve Bulgaristan dahil birçok ülkede bomba ihbarları nedeniyle 10'dan fazla yolcu uçağı acil iniş yaptı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Polonya'nın başkenti Varşova'dan Belçika'nın başkenti Brüksel'e giden uçak, bomba ihbarı üzerine Brüksel Havalimanı'na güvenli iniş gerçekleştirdi. Belçika federal polisi, incelemeler sonucunda herhangi bir ilave güvenlik önlemine gerek görülmediğini, olayın Avrupa'da son günlerde bazı uçaklar hakkında alınan bomba ihbarlarıyla bağlantılı olup olmadığına ilişkin soruşturma başlatıldığını bildirdi. Prag'a giden 4 uçağa yönelik bomba tehdidi Çekya polisi, başkent Prag'a giden 4 uçağa patlayıcı yerleştirildiği yönünde tehdit olduğunu açıkladı. Polis, ihbarların inandırıcılığının düşük değerlendirildiğini, buna rağmen durumun hafife alınmadığını ve havalimanı yetkilileriyle uçakların inişi için hazırlık yapıldığını bildirdi. Roma'ya giden 2 uçuşta da ihbar yapıldı Aer Lingus hava yolu şirketinin Dublin-Roma seferini yapan uçağı bomba ihbarı sebebiyle Fransa'daki Evreux Fauville Hava Üssü’ne acil iniş yapmak zorunda kaldı. 6 kişilik mürettebatın ve 151 yolcunun bulunduğu uçağın güvenli şekilde üsse iniş yaptığı ve durumun inceleme altında olduğu belirtildi. Finlandiya'nın Finnair hava yolu şirketinin Helsinki-Roma seferini yapan uçağı da bomba tehdidi olduğuna dair isimsiz ihbarların ardından İtalya Hava Kuvvetlerine ait savaş uçaklarının eşliğinde Roma Fiumicino Havalimanı'na iniş gerçekleştirdi. Salzburg'daki havalimanında geniş çaplı polis operasyonu Avusturya'nın Salzburg kentindeki havalimanında alınan ihbar nedeniyle geniş çaplı polis operasyonu başlatıldı. Polis ekipleri, havalimanının araç ve bina girişlerindeki güvenlik kontrollerini sıkılaştırdı. Polis sözcüsü, tehdidin rutin güvenlik prosedürleri kapsamında incelendiğini belirtirken havalimanı binası şu ana kadar tahliye edilmedi ve uçuşlarda aksama yaşanmadı. Polonya'nın ulusal hava yolu şirketi LOT'un başkent Varşova'daki Chopin Havalimanı'ndan Paris'e gerçekleştirdiği seferde kullanılan uçakla ilgili ihbar üzerine güvenlik prosedürleri uygulandı. Güvenlik prosedürleri kapsamında uçak ve bagajlar ilgili birimler tarafından ayrıntılı şekilde kontrol edilirken herhangi bir tehlikeli maddeye rastlanmadı. Londra-Sofya seferini gerçekleştiren ve 184 yolcu taşıyan uçak, öğle saatlerinde Filibe (Plovdiv) yakınlarındaki havalimanına iniş yaptı. Kopenhag ve Madrid'den gelen diğer iki uçağın ise başkent Sofya'daki Vasil Levski Havalimanı'na iniş yapacağı bildirildi. İhbarların hibrit saldırı olup olmadığı ve arkasında kimlerin bulunduğu araştırılıyor.

articles.title: Welsh aviation firm AerFin bought in £475m deal
articles.summary: The company, which was majority owned by a private equity firm, said it was beginning a "new chapter".
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Welsh aviation firm AerFin bought in £475m deal
articles.summaryTr: The company, which was majority owned by a private equity firm, said it was beginning a "new chapter".
articles.articleText: Welsh aviation firm AerFin bought in £475m deal - Published A Newport aviation company, that has grown into a global supplier of aircraft engines, parts and maintenance services, has been bought in a deal worth about £475m. Japanese firm ORIX Aviation has agreed to acquire AerFin, which employs more than 230 people and operates from sites in the UK and around the world. Founded by Bob James, AerFin has developed from a south Wales business into a global aviation aftermarket specialist. Announcing the takeover, AerFin described it as the start of a new chapter for the company. The firm - which was majority owned by a private equity company prior to the sale - buys, sells, leases and repairs aircraft, engines and components. In 2025, the company moved into a new purpose-built, 116,000 sq ft facility, external at Indurent Park in Newport. ORIX Aviation is the aircraft leasing arm of Japanese financial services giant the ORIX Group. Chief executive Simon Goodson called the acquisition a "defining moment" in the company's history. "I am delighted that AerFin is joining the ORIX Group, a business that shares our values and belief in trusted partnerships, flexible solutions and finding the way ahead for our customers," he said. He said support from the wider ORIX Group would provide "the confidence and platform" to grow the aviation business. "This is a defining moment in AerFin's story and the beginning of an exciting new chapter," said Goodson. AerFin has built its existing business around extending the life of aircraft and engines through trading, leasing, repair and reuse. It helps airlines and aviation companies source parts and manage assets. The company claims to serve more than 600 organisations. For ORIX Aviation, the acquisition expands its activities beyond aircraft ownership and leasing, into aftermarket services and end-of-life aircraft management. The company said the combination would strengthen its capabilities across the entire lifecycle of an aircraft. James Meyler, chief executive of ORIX Aviation, said AerFin had built "a leading aviation aftermarket platform" supported by extensive technical expertise and an international customer base. The sale also marks the exit of Danish private equity investor CataCap, which had been the majority shareholder in AerFin. Founder Bob James said he was pleased to see the business move to what he described as "a long-term home", capable of supporting AerFin's next phase of expansion. "I recognise a strong leadership team and a long-term home when I see one," James said. Related topics More top stories - Published6 hours ago - Published1 day ago

articles.articleText: Was an Italian chef really fired over refusal to put pineapple on pizza? Italian chef Davide Tamburella was fired from a Brisbane restaurant in May after the establishment's management expressed concerns about a string of complaints about the chef's behaviour. Among them were Tamburella's refusal to provide ham and pineapple pizza for guests at a function. It was the third time Tamburella had refused to use the fruit on pizzas in the past four years. At the time, the chef had stated that putting pineapple on pizza was "offensive to his culture". Australia correspondent Katy Watson explains what led to Tamburella's dismissal.

articles.title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation
articles.summary: Five of France's unions have joined a wave of strikes and protests in a national day of action.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation
articles.summaryTr: Five of France's unions have joined a wave of strikes and protests in a national day of action.
articles.articleText: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation - Published Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators are expected to take part in marches across France as five unions join strikes and protests in a national day of action. The protests began in September with high school students complaining about poor conditions and resources in education, but have spread to include the so-called "yellow-vest" movement and workers. Authorities expect 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators to join marches, with tens of thousands more in Paris alone, in a day billed by one union leader as "a great day of convergence". The five unions have combined forces across the public and private sector, with demands for higher wages to combat the cost of living and protected public services. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has said that 70,000 police and gendarmes are being deployed, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence. More than 250 separate actions are planned for 5 November, with some disruption reported in schools, hospitals and public transport. Workers have also been asked to halt production at oil refineries, and France is expected to import more electricity than it produces on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants. A coalition of unions has urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour. The head of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase: "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month." The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028. Some 81 lycées - high schools that cater for 15-18 year-olds - were shut on Thursday morning, according to the education ministry. It added that about 17.5% of primary schools too were affected by the strikes. Large numbers are expected on the streets, especially in the capital, and Léon said she would be happy if 800,000 people turned out. One union leader Sophie Binet, who called it the "great day of convergence", added: "The time has come to take the mobilisation to the next level; the strike must take over." Meanwhile, a revived gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement that staged a revolt against the high cost of living several years ago has called for further blockades and protests on Friday and Saturday too. Union leaders have complained that recent marches have been kept away from the centre of Paris, because of violence that broke out in towns and cities on 17 October and led to more than 2,000 stores being looted and historic buildings being set on fire. Thursday's march will be allowed through the centre of Paris, although not along the route proposed by the unions between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Concorde, which would have taken protesters near the National Assembly, the Élysée Palace, and the prime minister's residence at Hôtel Matignon. Instead, the march is set to follow another central route from Place de la République to Place de la Nation. The CFDT union complained that getting court approval for the route only on Wednesday evening made organising the march more difficult. The last big mobilisation at the weekend passed off with relatively little violence, and the interior minister said the police deployment would be on a similar scale on Thursday. Nuñez has spoken of three potential risks on Thursday, from radical left "black blocs" groups and looting to wildcat marches without union authorisation. - Published4 days ago

Workers have also been asked to halt production at oil refineries, and France is expected to import more electricity than it produces on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants. A coalition of unions has urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour. The head of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase: "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month." The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028. Some 81 lycées - high schools that cater for 15-18 year-olds - were shut on Thursday morning, according to the education ministry. It added that about 17.5% of primary schools too were affected by the strikes. Large numbers are expected on the streets, especially in the capital, and Léon said she would be happy if 800,000 people turned out. One union leader Sophie Binet, who called it the "great day of convergence", added: "The time has come to take the mobilisation to the next level; the strike must take over." Union leaders have complained that recent marches have been kept away from the centre of Paris, because of violence that broke out in towns and cities on 17 October and led to more than 2,000 stores being looted and historic buildings being set on fire. Thursday's march will be allowed through the centre of Paris, although not along the route proposed by the unions between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Concorde, which would have taken protesters near the National Assembly, the Élysée Palace, and the prime minister's residence at Hôtel Matignon. Instead, the march is set to follow another central route from Place de la République to Place de la Nation. The CFDT union complained that getting court approval for the route only on Wednesday evening made organising the march more difficult. The last big mobilisation at the weekend passed off with relatively little violence, and the interior minister said the police deployment would be on a similar scale on Thursday. Nuñez has spoken of three potential risks on Thursday, from radical left "black blocs" groups and looting to wildcat marches without union authorisation. - Published4 days ago

articles.title: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown
articles.summary: A consultation will consider fines and other ways to clamp down on dangerous e-bike riders.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown
articles.summaryTr: A consultation will consider fines and other ways to clamp down on dangerous e-bike riders.
articles.articleText: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown - Published People riding drunk or dangerously on e-bikes – and those who jump red lights - could face on-the-spot fines under plans to curb anti-social behaviour. Firms which run shared e-bike schemes will also be expected to manage their fleets better and provide designated parking areas to keep pavements safe. They could also be required to take out insurance so people can claim compensation if they are hit by someone on a shared bike. It's part of a crackdown on what ministers called the "wild west" of e-biking – with a patchwork of rules across the country often leaving the streets unsafe for pedestrians. A consultation launched on Thursday sets out proposed national standards to make journeys safer for everyone and keep pavements clear, particularly for wheelchair users and families with prams. The first e-bikes were launched in Exeter in 2016 and arrived in London a year later, growing to become a popular commuter option. According to the Greater London Authority, 37 million trips were taken on dockless e-bikes last year – a third more than the previous year. Shared e-bikes - such as Lime, Voi, Beryl, Dott, Forest and Bolt - make short journeys quick and convenient. While some areas enforce rules that mean shared bikes can only be left in specific areas, others have looser rules. Under the government's proposals, local leaders will be able to license schemes in their area, allowing them to enforce minimum standards and better integrate e-bikes into existing transport networks. Measures could include requiring operators to have a parking plan and to manage fleet sizes and operating areas, so bikes aren't overcrowding streets. The consultation will also consider ways to tackle antisocial and illegal behaviour, to prevent users from riding shared cycles drunk, underage, or on pavements. There will also be clear consequences set out – such as fines for this type of behaviour. The government is also consulting on whether local leaders should have extra powers, including setting fees and requirements for operators to share data to improve enforcement and journey planning. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the e-bike clampdown was a "small but important everyday fix" which would make streets safer. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said the changes would "stop nuisance parking, tackle antisocial behaviour and make journeys safer". Bosses at Lime, Voi and Bolt all welcomed the proposals, adding that consistent standards being applied across the country would provide clarity and certainty for operators, riders and the general public. articles.title: Second buyer makes rescue bid for Poundland as retailer faces collapse
articles.summary: A little-known investment group has made a bid to buy the business.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Second buyer makes rescue bid for Poundland as retailer faces collapse
articles.summaryTr: A little-known investment group has made a bid to buy the business.
articles.articleText: Second buyer makes rescue bid for Poundland as retailer faces collapse - Published A second buyer has made a rescue bid for Poundland as the discount retailer teeters on the brink of collapse, with thousands of jobs at risk. London-based Xyra Group has offered to pay off half of Poundland's outstanding debts - a key sticking point in takeover talks so far - immediately. The rest would be deferred. With Poundland close to collapse, US-based owners Gordon Brothers have already rejected a rival bid from an Irish property group which would have saved its 12,000 staff. Gordon Brothers said the business has faced years of instability and "remains challenged and vulnerable". Sources familiar with the offer said Xyra is offering to immediately pay off £12.5m of an outstanding £30m loan on Poundland's books. The offer came as Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds held crunch talks with Gordon Brothers about the future of the business, urging the investment firm to protect staff however possible. Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, committed at the meeting to prioritise offers which protect its shops and workers. The company said: "We are pursuing all avenues through the sale process to find a solution which protects as many jobs as possible and preserves value. Work continues at pace, engaging in active discussions on offers with interested parties." Xyra is offering to pay off a higher proportion of Poundland's outstanding debts than Martin Property Group, which previously submitted a bid that Gordon Brothers rejected. But doubts remain about the credibility of Xyra's offer, as there is little evidence they meet Gordon Brothers' tests, including whether they have the money and whether they would be good long-term owners of Poundland. Sources pointed to the appointment of Andrew Brode to Xyra's board as a sign of its credibility. Brode works for RWS - a company that provides AI solutions for businesses. Judith MacKenzie, head of Downing Fund Managers, told the BBC Brode is "well known and very credible" among small businesses in the UK. But she said there is "hardly any information" publicly available about Xyra. "So, although some of the people look good, I can't find any evidence to say that they've got the money to back it up yet," MacKenzie added. Gordon Brothers said: "Our intent throughout the comprehensive sale process has been to protect as many jobs as possible and preserve value in order to deliver the best available outcome for all the people, creditors and local communities who care about this business as much as we do." Both Reynolds and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have questioned why a deal for the future of Poundland has not yet been made. Though Xyra made an offer to take over the whole business, it is unclear whether it would keep Poundland together as its owner or break the company up. Several Poundland suppliers have said they would also go bust if the retailer collapses. Its founder Steve Smith said two or three thousand suppliers to the firm, those who solely work for Poundland, would be caught up in the collapse. He added that not only would Poundland's 12,000 staff be affected in that case, but potentially up to 30,000 overall. Related topics - Published2 days ago - Published5 hours ago

articles.title: South Korea seeks 4th crypto tax delay, targets 2029 start
articles.summary: South Korea is seeking a fourth delay to its 22% crypto tax, months after reaffirming plans to begin taxing digital asset gains in January 2027.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: South Korea seeks 4th crypto tax delay, targets 2029 start
articles.summaryTr: South Korea is seeking a fourth delay to its 22% crypto tax, months after reaffirming plans to begin taxing digital asset gains in January 2027.
articles.articleText: South Korea seeks 4th crypto tax delay, targets 2029 start South Korea is seeking a fourth delay to its 22% crypto tax, months after reaffirming plans to begin taxing digital asset gains in January 2027. South Korea’s government has backed postponing tax on cryptocurrency gains by another two years to 2029, in what would be the fourth delay to its implementation. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il announced the proposal Thursday, saying the government would consult lawmakers on postponing the January 2027 implementation date. The tax would impose a 22% levy, comprising a 20% income tax and 2% local tax, on annual crypto gains exceeding 2.5 million won ($1,860). The government cited 2029 as the start of information exchange with the US under the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). It said imposing the tax before those exchanges begin could put the domestic market at a disadvantage relative to overseas markets. It also wants to account for changes under planned digital asset legislation. Officials also said they plan to introduce a three-year loss carryforward provision, allowing investors to offset crypto losses against profits earned over the following three years. The government plans to submit amendments to improve the tax system during parliament’s regular session in 2027, with detailed tax guidelines planned for the first half of 2028. The tax was originally scheduled to take effect in January 2022 but was subsequently postponed to 2023, 2025 and 2027. The proposal reverses the government’s previous position. A Finance Ministry official said in May that implementation would proceed in 2027. South Korean finance officials recently engaged with major crypto exchanges amid growing calls to postpone the tax. Industry representatives cited unresolved tax rules for different transaction types and insufficient time to prepare the necessary infrastructure. Related: South Korea plans cybersecurity overhaul after attacks hit banks, crypto firms

articles.title: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics
articles.summary: Easily the most anticipated Bollywood film of the year, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two parts.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics
articles.summaryTr: Easily the most anticipated Bollywood film of the year, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two parts.
articles.articleText: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics - Published India's most expensive film - a lavish retelling of the Hindu epic Ramayana, made in two parts for a reported $500m (£370m) - has opened in cinemas worldwide, sparking enormous expectations and mixed reviews. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two planned films, a sprawling production that brings together some of India's biggest stars, Hollywood visual-effects expertise and two Oscar-winning composers in an attempt to take one of the country's most revered stories to a global audience. One of Hinduism's foundational epics, the Ramayana has travelled across centuries and continents, finding expression in poetry, temple sculpture, shadow puppetry, folk theatre and stories passed down through generations. It has outlasted kingdoms and empires, inspired religious devotion and political movements, and found new life, again and again, on TV and in cinema. Tiwari's version returns to the familiar story of love, duty, exile and war, set in a world of gods and demons, celestial weapons and mighty kingdoms. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Ram, the virtuous prince of Ayodhya. Banished from his kingdom for 14 years, he retreats to the forest with his wife Sita (played by Sai Pallavi), who is kidnapped by Ravana, the 10-headed king of Lanka. Played by Yash, one of southern India's biggest stars, Ravana is a powerful warrior whose pride leads him into an epic battle with Ram (which will be depicted in part 2, set to release next year). The film's producer, Namit Malhotra, heads visual-effects company DNEG, which has worked on Hollywood blockbusters including Dune and Interstellar. The music is a collaboration between AR Rahman, the Oscar-winning Indian composer of Slumdog Millionaire, and Hans Zimmer, whose scores for Gladiator, The Dark Knight and Dune have helped define the sound of modern Hollywood. The film opened days ahead of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights which celebrates Ram's return to Ayodhya after his exile. But the critical response so far has been mixed. Saibal Chatterjee of NDTV channel gave it, external three out of five stars, saying its visual spectacle often overshadowed the story. Its enormous scale, he wrote, "remains, for the most part, the only thing that stands out", while the acting remains "wildly inconsistent". Rishabh Suri of the Hindustan Times newspaper was more enthusiastic, awarding it four stars. "I am happy to report, all that money shows on screen," he wrote, praising the performances and visual effects, though he found the first half sluggish and the music underwhelming. Shubhra Gupta, external of The Indian Express, who gave the film three stars, confessed to initial misgivings about its extravagant scale but found herself gradually won over, calling it the "perfect epic". There was "enough sorcery and thrills and adventure" to sustain the spectacle, she wrote, and the filmmakers had managed to tell a sprawling story without being swallowed by it. Internationally, too, the film drew contrasting reactions. Writing in The Guardian, Peter Bradshaw called it a "thoroughly engaging, rousing and spectacular Indian epic melodrama". He found echoes of Shakespeare in the royal intrigue that sends Rama into exile, and of Homer in his quest to rescue Sita. Its sweeping landscapes and fantastical imagery reminded him of The Lord of the Rings and The Lion King. "It's a rather amazing adventure," he wrote, external, giving it four stars. Others were less impressed. Siddhant Adlakha of IGN scored the film four out of 10, describing its action as "clunky" and its computer-generated imagery as an "eye-sore". Giovanni Lago of Next Best Picture, who gave it, external five out of 10, praised Yash's magnetic Ravana and the score by Rahman and Zimmer. But he felt the film's vast narrative might have been better served by a Game of Thrones-style series. The use of AI to adjust actors' lip movements for the English-language version also drew criticism. While Tiwari said it was intended to make the film more accessible to international audiences, Adlakha likened the result to "exaggerated mouth movements superimposed on still images for comedy sketches". In India, the film has invited comparisons with earlier adaptations, particularly Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan, which captivated the country nearly four decades ago with simple sets and special effects that now seem quaint. When the series first aired in 1987, Sunday mornings across India took on an almost devotional stillness. Streets emptied, shops lowered their shutters and neighbours crowded around TV sets. Some viewers bathed, lit incense and garlanded their screens before the broadcast, preparing for the show much as they might for worship. Arvind Rajagopal, a media scholar at New York University, told the BBC in 2019 that trains and buses would stop and passengers disembark to watch the show on roadside TVs. Broadcast on the state-run Doordarshan network, some of the most popular parts of the 78-episode series drew an estimated 80-100 million viewers, astonishing numbers at a time when owning a TV was a luxury in India. The actors, too, became objects of reverence. Arun Govil, who played Ram, has recalled people weeping at the sight of him and touching his feet. Now, in a casting choice brimming with nostalgia, Govil returns in Tiwari's film as Dasharatha, Ram's father. Other adaptations found their own ways to reimagine the epic. The 1992 Indo-Japanese animated film Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Rama brought the tale to life through richly detailed, hand-drawn animation. Tiwari's Ramayana arrives with technological resources its predecessors could barely have imagined - but also with the expectations of generations who have grown up with the story and its characters. It also comes at a politically charged moment in India, where Ram has become a powerful symbol of Hindu identity - over the past decade and a half, even popular analyses or retellings of the epic have landed in controversy. The 2023 film Adipurush, another big-budget retelling of Ramayana, sparked backlash on several fronts. Hindu groups called for a ban, accusing it of disrespecting religious figures, while some critics questioned its depiction of Ravana, which they said drew on Mughal imagery and reinforced stereotypes about Muslims. The film was also criticised for its dialogue and visual effects. For the actors portraying these characters in the latest film, that burden was deeply felt. "I was filled with fear," Kapoor told the BBC Asian Network's Haroon Rashid. "I knew that maybe I'm too old for this. I won't be able to do justice to it." He called the role "an opportunity of a lifetime", but said playing a figure worshipped by millions left little room for the creative freedom he had enjoyed in other films. Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita, said the experience was as much spiritual as artistic. Raised in a religious household, she said she approached the part not just as a performance, but as an opportunity for personal growth. How the film is being received will become clearer soon, as audiences head to cinemas. But whatever the verdict, it marks a major cultural moment for India, bringing a story loved for generations to the big screen on an unprecedented scale.

It also comes at a politically charged moment in India, where Ram has become a powerful symbol of Hindu identity - over the past decade and a half, even popular analyses or retellings of the epic have landed in controversy. The 2023 film Adipurush, another big-budget retelling of Ramayana, sparked backlash on several fronts. Hindu groups called for a ban, accusing it of disrespecting religious figures, while some critics questioned its depiction of Ravana, which they said drew on Mughal imagery and reinforced stereotypes about Muslims. The film was also criticised for its dialogue and visual effects. For the actors portraying these characters in the latest film, that burden was deeply felt. "I was filled with fear," Kapoor told the BBC Asian Network's Haroon Rashid. "I knew that maybe I'm too old for this. I won't be able to do justice to it." He called the role "an opportunity of a lifetime", but said playing a figure worshipped by millions left little room for the creative freedom he had enjoyed in other films. Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita, said the experience was as much spiritual as artistic. Raised in a religious household, she said she approached the part not just as a performance, but as an opportunity for personal growth. How the film is being received will become clearer soon, as audiences head to cinemas. But whatever the verdict, it marks a major cultural moment for India, bringing a story loved for generations to the big screen on an unprecedented scale.

articles.titleTr: France budget rejection sidelines stablecoin tax, wallet reporting
articles.summaryTr: Three adopted amendments, including stablecoin taxation and self-custody reporting, fall away but could be reintroduced in the Senate.
articles.articleText: France budget rejection sidelines stablecoin tax, wallet reporting Three adopted amendments, including stablecoin taxation and self-custody reporting, fall away but could be reintroduced in the Senate. The French National Assembly rejected the 2027 state budget’s revenue section late Wednesday, removing crypto-related amendments from the version of the bill sent to the Senate. The Assembly rejected the revenue section by a vote of 458–0 at first reading, with two abstentions, according to the official voting record. The revenue section covers government income, such as taxes. After the rejection, the government will send the Senate the original budget text, without the crypto-related amendments adopted by lawmakers. The proposals could still be reintroduced in the Senate and would need to survive the remaining budget process to become law. Faustine Fleuret, global head of public affairs at lending protocol Morpho, told Cointelegraph before the vote that rejection of the revenue section could “result in the rejection of the entire bill in the National Assembly, including provisions adopted by way of amendments.” Self-custody reporting and stablecoin tax proposals fall away The Assembly adopted three crypto-related amendments before rejecting the revenue section. On Oct. 16, lawmakers adopted an amendment that would make gains from crypto-to-stablecoin conversions taxable. On Tuesday, lawmakers adopted another amendment that would require taxpayers to disclose self-custodied crypto holdings totaling at least 100,000 euros ($112,000), with the threshold assessed on Dec. 31 of the tax year. Another amendment would increase penalties from 10,000 euros to 50,000 euros for crypto platforms failing to provide information requested by tax authorities. The Senate is scheduled to begin debating the finance bill on Nov. 20, followed by an examination of the revenue section’s articles on Nov. 23, according to its schedule. Related: EU investors rank crypto above retirement plans for lasting wealth creation: OKX survey

articles.summary: Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law.

articles.titleTr: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
articles.summaryTr: Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law.
articles.articleText: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years - Published Joshua Wong, once the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, has been sentenced to 10 years in jail for colluding with foreign forces under the city's sweeping national security law. Wong is among hundreds of campaigners and ordinary Hongkongers arrested under the law, which was imposed in 2020 following explosive pro-democracy protests against Beijing's growing control. Critics say the far-reaching law has silenced dissent, but authorities argue that it is needed to maintain stability and deny it has weakened the city's cherished autonomy. Having already spent the last six years in jail, Wong, who was due to be freed in January, will now spend another decade behind bars. - Silenced and erased, Hong Kong's decade of protest is now a defiant memory - Published30 November 2024 - What a defiant mogul's trial says about Hong Kong - Published18 December 2023 Wong, who turned 30 last month, has already been imprisoned multiple times for his activism which started when he was a teen. On Thursday, he arrived in court wearing a dark blue long-sleeved shirt, khaki trousers and black-rimmed glasses. He looked slimmer compared to his previous public appearances. He nodded in greeting towards members of the packed public gallery, and took notes intermittently as the judge read out the reasons for his sentencing. A crowd had gathered outside the court, with dozens of Hongkongers having queued for hours hoping to get a seat in the public gallery. There was also a heavy police presence. Wong is already serving time for subversion and was due to be freed early next year when he was handed the latest charges, which he has pleaded guilty to earlier in September. Two months and two days of the 10-year term will be served concurrently with his ongoing sentence, the judge said on Thursday. Prosecutors said that Wong had conspired with other campaigners, including self-exiled activist Nathan Law, to lobby for foreign sanctions and blockades against Beijing. These activities took place between July and late November 2020, the court heard. Wong and Law had been co-founders of Demosisto, a now defunct pro-democracy political party. On Thursday, Hong Kong's chief executive John Lee said Wong and Law were "among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong's prosperity and stability". Their actions "not only severely undermined national sovereignty, security, and development interests, but also directly prejudiced the well-being of the general public and the stability of society," Lee said in a statement issued after the ruling. Beijing's foreign ministry said China "firmly supports [Hong Kong] in safeguarding national security in accordance with the law". It also called on "relevant parties" to "earnestly respect China's sovereignty and Hong Kong's legal system". Wong's friend and fellow activist Frances Hui, now based in the US, says she is "heartbroken" and "outraged" by the verdict. "Today's sentencing is not just about Joshua. It is part of a broader political crackdown that seeks to rewrite a chapter of Hong Kong's history and erase the contributions of an entire generation who believed they could shape the future of their city," she told the BBC. Human Rights Watch described the ruling as "cruel and unjust". "To keep Hong Kong society subdued, and to reduce the chance of an international outcry, the Hong Kong government appears to have adopted the tactic of stacking charges against influential pro-democracy leaders," said its Asia director Elaine Pearson. The harshest sentence under the controversial national security law (NSL) thus far has been handed to former media tycoon Jimmy Lai, who was jailed for 20 years, also for colluding with foreign forces. Who is Joshua Wong? Born to IT professional Roger and homemaker Grace in October 1996, Wong was diagnosed with dyslexia as a child, which made him struggle with school. However, he was quick to challenge established rules and norms when they didn't make sense. In secondary school, he rallied with his classmates to protest against the high prices of canteen lunches on Facebook. In 2011, Wong, then 14, co-founded the pro-democracy student activist group Scholarism, which quickly grew in size and influence. The following year, the group rallied more than 100,000 people to protest against Hong Kong's plans to implement mandatory "patriotic education" in schools, forcing the authorities to back down. By 2014, Wong, who was then at the forefront of a civil disobedience movement known as the "Umbrella Movement", had already become one of the most recognisable faces of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement. In 2016, he co-founded Demosisto with Law and Agnes Chow, an activist who is now also in exile. But he often expressed discomfort at being labelled a "protest leader". "We have a lot of facilitators in this movement and I'm one of them... Instead of having a top-down command, we now have a bottom-up command hub," Wong told The Financial Times in November 2019. Demosisto disbanded in 2020, the year Beijing introduced the NSL in Hong Kong. Law left for the UK and continued his advocacy abroad, while Wong stayed on in Hong Kong and tried to run for a seat in its legislature – but was barred, with authorities citing his opposition to the NSL as one of the reasons. Meanwhile, the court cases against Wong were stacking up. On 23 November 2020, he pleaded guilty to several charges related to his involvement in protests outside the Hong Kong police headquarters in 2019. Then came the NSL charges. While still in prison in February 2021, Wong was among 47 people charged with "conspiracy to commit subversion". The group became known as the Hong Kong 47 and remains the largest prosecution so far under the NSL. Wong was still serving his 56-month sentence for the subversion conviction when he was charged with collusion under the NSL last year. On 22 November 2020, the day before he pleaded guilty to the protest charges, Wong wrote in a post on Instagram addressed to "the people of Hong Kong": "To be honest, I have never had much faith in Hong Kong's politics, but I have every confidence in the people of Hong Kong. "Even as political power now poses a comprehensive challenge to the resilience of our civil society, I believe the people of Hong Kong will, as always, find a way to see things through." articles.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
articles.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball
articles.articleText: Release Number 9314-26 CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball October 26, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the National Basketball Association today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to protect the integrity of professional basketball in prediction markets. Through the MOU, the CFTC and NBA will better share information by regularly communicating and discussing matters relating to integrity, as well as maintaining fair and transparent prediction markets. “I’m pleased the CFTC and NBA signed an MOU which continues the Commission’s commitment to increasing data sharing between the agency and professional sports leagues,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The NBA joins the MLB and NHL in taking a responsible step toward protecting sports integrity and market participants from abuses in prediction markets like insider trading and fraud. I thank NBA Commissioner Adam Silver for putting the integrity of professional basketball and America’s financial markets first and for working with the CFTC on this MOU.” -CFTC-

news.summary: Bankacılık sektörünün toplam mevduatı 30 Ekim haftasında geriledi. Sektörün toplam mevduatı 34 trilyon 105 milyar liraya inerken, kredi hacmi 28 trilyon 222,3 milyar liraya yükseldi. Bankacılık sektörünün toplam kredi hacminin 30 Ekim itibarıyla 29 trilyon lirayı geçtiği bildirildi.

news.titleTr: Bankacılık sektörünün mevduatı azaldı, kredi hacmi arttı

news.articleText: Bankacılık sektörünün mevduatı azaldı, kredi hacmi arttı - Bankacılık sektörünün toplam mevduatı 30 Ekim haftasında geriledi. Sektörün toplam mevduatı 34 trilyon 105 milyar liraya inerken, kredi hacmi 28 trilyon 222,3 milyar liraya yükseldi. - Bankacılık sektörünün toplam kredi hacminin 30 Ekim itibarıyla 29 trilyon lirayı geçtiği bildirildi. Bankacılık sektörünün toplam mevduatı, 30 Ekim ile biten haftada bir önceki haftaya göre 109 milyar 731 milyon 981 bin lira azalışla 34 trilyon 105 milyar 40 milyon 447 bin liraya geriledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB), haftalık para ve banka istatistiklerini açıkladı. Buna göre, bankacılık sektörünün toplam mevduatı 30 Ekim ile biten haftada yüzde 0,32 azalarak 34 trilyon 214 milyar 772 milyon 427 bin liradan 34 trilyon 105 milyar 40 milyon 447 bin liraya indi. Aynı dönemde yurt içi yerleşiklerin bankalardaki Türk lirası cinsi mevduatı yüzde 0,73 azalışla 18 trilyon 821 milyar 273 milyon 181 bin lira, yabancı para (YP) cinsinden mevduatı yüzde 0,12 artışla 11 trilyon 116 milyar 49 milyon 354 bin lira oldu. Bankalarda bulunan toplam YP mevduatı geçen hafta 261 milyar 248 milyon 15 bin dolar düzeyinde gerçekleşirken, bu tutarın 223 milyar 806 milyon 596 bin doları yurt içinde yerleşik kişilerin hesaplarında toplandı. Yurt içi yerleşiklerin toplam YP mevduatında parite etkisinden arındırılmış veriler dikkate alındığında, 30 Ekim itibarıyla 585 milyon 115 bin dolarlık artış görüldü. Yurt içi yerleşiklerin tüketici kredileri arttı Bankacılık sektöründe yurt içi yerleşiklerin tüketici kredileri, geçen hafta yüzde 1,65 artışla 7 trilyon 45 milyar 268 milyon 641 bin liraya yükseldi. Söz konusu kredilerin 851 milyar 747 milyon 604 bin lirası konut, 42 milyar 584 milyon 455 bin lirası taşıt, 2 trilyon 654 milyar 930 milyon 37 bin lirası ihtiyaç kredileri, 3 trilyon 496 milyar 6 milyon 545 bin lirası ise bireysel kredi kartlarından oluştu. Bankacılık sektörünün toplam kredi hacmi de 30 Ekim ile biten haftada 227 milyar 635 milyon 866 bin lira artarak 27 trilyon 994 milyar 642 milyon 833 bin liradan 28 trilyon 222 milyar 278 milyon 699 bin liraya yükseldi. Bankacılık sektörünün kredi hacmi 29 trilyon lirayı aştı Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumunun (BDDK) yayımladığı haftalık bültene göre, bankacılık sektörünün toplam kredi hacmi 30 Ekim itibarıyla 224 milyar 223 milyon lira artarak 28 trilyon 776 milyar 556 milyon liradan 29 trilyon 779 milyon liraya çıktı. Bankacılık sektöründe toplam mevduat ise bankalar arası dahil, geçen hafta 112 milyar 999 milyon lira azalarak 32 trilyon 852 milyar 309 milyon liradan 32 trilyon 739 milyar 311 milyon liraya geriledi. Tüketici kredileri 3 trilyon 557 milyar liraya yükseldi Tüketici kredilerinin tutarı, bu dönemde 32 milyar 405 milyon lira artarak 3 trilyon 556 milyar 940 milyon liraya çıktı. Bu tutarın 852 milyar 509 milyon lirası konut, 42 milyar 729 milyon lirası taşıt ve 2 trilyon 661 milyar 701 milyon lirası ihtiyaç kredilerinden oluştu. Bu dönemde taksitli ticari kredilerin tutarı 1 trilyon 173 milyar 2 milyon lira artarak 5 trilyon 522 milyar 843 milyon lira oldu. Bankaların bireysel kredi kartı alacakları ise 82 milyar 115 milyon lira artışla 3 trilyon 496 milyar 309 milyon lira düzeyinde gerçekleşti. Bireysel kredi kartı alacaklarının 1 trilyon 298 milyar 714 milyon lirasını taksitli, 2 trilyon 197 milyar 595 milyon lirasını taksitsiz borçlar oluşturdu. Yasal öz kaynaklar arttı Bankacılık sektöründe takipteki alacaklar, 30 Ekim itibarıyla önceki haftaya göre 18 milyar 34 milyon lira artışla 983 milyar 118 milyon liraya çıktı. Takipteki alacakların 709 milyar 184 milyon lirasına özel karşılık ayrıldı. Aynı dönemde bankacılık sisteminin yasal öz kaynakları 23 milyar 894 milyon lira artarak 6 trilyon 210 milyar 913 milyon liraya yükseldi.

news.title: BIST 100'de yükseliş devam edecek mi? Tuna Çetinkaya 5 sektöre işaret etti

news.titleTr: BIST 100'de yükseliş devam edecek mi? Tuna Çetinkaya 5 sektöre işaret etti
news.summaryTr: Borsa İstanbul'daki yükselişi değerlendiren Kuzey Menkul Değerler Genel Müdürü Tuna Çetinkaya, BIST 100'de 11.500 puanın üzerinde kalıcılığın kritik olduğunu belirtti. Kayıpların telafi edilebileceğini söyleyen Çetinkaya, yatırımcıların dikkatini çekebilecek 5 sektöre işaret etti.
news.articleText: BIST 100'de yükseliş devam edecek mi? Tuna Çetinkaya 5 sektöre işaret etti Borsa İstanbul'daki yükselişi değerlendiren Kuzey Menkul Değerler Genel Müdürü Tuna Çetinkaya, BIST 100'de 11.500 puanın üzerinde kalıcılığın kritik olduğunu belirtti. Kayıpların telafi edilebileceğini söyleyen Çetinkaya, yatırımcıların dikkatini çekebilecek 5 sektöre işaret etti. Kuzey Menkul Değerler Genel Müdürü Tuna Çetinkaya, CNBC-e'de Şafak Tükle'nin sunduğu Açılış Öncesi programında Borsa İstanbul'daki son yükselişi, BIST 100 endeksinin teknik görünümünü ve yıl sonuna ilişkin beklentilerini değerlendirdi. ABD'deki ara seçimlerin ardından küresel piyasalarda artan risk iştahının Türkiye piyasalarına da olumlu yansıdığını belirten Çetinkaya, Borsa İstanbul'da son günlerde yaşanan yükselişte fon piyasasına ilişkin belirsizliklerin azalmasının etkili olduğunu söyledi. BIST 100 endeksinin 11.500 puan seviyesini yeniden test etmesini değerlendiren Çetinkaya, teknik açıdan bir dönüş sinyali oluşabilmesi için bazı koşulların yerine gelmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Çetinkaya, endeksin haftayı olumlu tamamlamasının ve 11.500 puanın üzerinde destek oluşturmasının önemli olduğunu belirterek bu seviyede kalıcılık sağlanması gerektiğini ifade etti. Borsa İstanbul'da sert fiyat hareketleri yerine daha dengeli bir yükselişe ihtiyaç duyulduğunu dile getiren Çetinkaya, volatilitenin azalmasının yatırımcı güveninin yeniden oluşması açısından önem taşıdığını söyledi. BIST 100'de kayıplar telafi edilebilir BIST 100 endeksinin son bir ayda yaklaşık yüzde 7'ye yakın değer kaybettiğine dikkat çeken Çetinkaya, bu kaybın önümüzdeki birkaç hafta içerisinde telafi edilebileceğini öngördü. Yıl sonuna doğru piyasanın daha olumlu bir görünüm sergileyebileceğini belirten Çetinkaya, son dönemde yaşanan maddi ve psikolojik kayıpların etkisinin zamanla azalabileceğini ifade etti. Çetinkaya, mevcut yükselişi ilk aşamada bir tepki hareketi olarak değerlendirdiğini ancak piyasalardaki iyimserliğin devam etme ihtimalini daha güçlü gördüğünü söyledi. Borsada yeni yükselişin başlangıcı mı? Borsa İstanbul'da yaşanan sert satışların ardından birçok şirketin değerleme açısından cazip seviyelere gerilediğini belirten Çetinkaya, bazı hisselerin defter değerlerinin altında işlem gördüğüne dikkat çekti. Fon piyasasında yaşanan sorunların yalnızca ilgili hisseleri değil, güçlü şirketlerin paylarını da olumsuz etkilediğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, kredilerin geri çağrılması ve likidite sıkışıklığının satış baskısını artırdığını söyledi. Bu süreçte ortaya çıkan fiyatlamaların orta ve uzun vadeli yatırımcılar açısından fırsata dönüşebileceğini belirten Çetinkaya, mevcut toparlanmanın yeni bir yükseliş döneminin başlangıcı olabileceğini ancak bunun için piyasada dengelenmenin sağlanması gerektiğini vurguladı. Bazı hisselerde yüzde 60'a varan kayıplar yaşandı BIST 30, BIST 50 ve BIST 100 kapsamındaki bazı hisselerde zirve seviyelere göre yüzde 40 ila yüzde 60 arasında değer kayıpları yaşandığını belirten Çetinkaya, bu kayıpların tamamının geri alınmasının beklenmemesi gerektiğini söyledi. Güçlü bilançolara sahip bazı şirketlerin kayıplarını daha kısa sürede telafi edebileceğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, yatırımcıların hisse seçiminde daha dikkatli davranması gerektiğine işaret etti. Çetinkaya, özellikle bankacılık, holding, sanayi, iletişim ve perakende sektörlerindeki büyük ve güçlü şirketlerin öne çıkabileceğini belirtti. Borsa İstanbul'da son günlerde yaşanan yükselişin önemli nedenlerinden birinin fon piyasasındaki belirsizliklerin azalması olduğunu belirten Çetinkaya, tasfiye sürecindeki fonlara ait hisselerin borsa dışında satılmasına yönelik gelişmelerin satış baskısını hafiflettiğini söyledi. Piyasada yaşanan sürecin yatırımcılar ve aracı kurumlar üzerinde ciddi etkiler bıraktığını ifade eden Çetinkaya, normalleşmenin başladığına ilişkin işaretler görüldüğünü ancak güvenin yeniden sağlanmasının zaman alacağını vurguladı. Yıl sonu için iyimser beklenti Küresel piyasalardaki olumlu havanın Türkiye açısından da önemli fırsatlar oluşturabileceğini belirten Çetinkaya, özellikle petrol fiyatlarında yaşanabilecek gerilemenin enflasyonla mücadeleyi destekleyebileceğini söyledi. Enerji maliyetlerindeki olası düşüşün Türkiye ekonomisine olumlu yansıyabileceğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, aralık ayında Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasının faiz indirimine gitme ihtimalinin de takip edileceğini belirtti. Borsa İstanbul'daki toparlanmanın devam edebileceğini ancak bunun sağlıklı bir yükselişe dönüşmesi için teknik seviyelerde kalıcılık, azalan oynaklık ve yatırımcı güveninin yeniden güçlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.

news.summary: See the maps and charts that show how America voted in the US midterm elections.

news.titleTr: How America voted in maps and charts
news.summaryTr: See the maps and charts that show how America voted in the US midterm elections.
news.articleText: How America voted in maps and charts - Published It's been an extraordinary night for the Democrats in the US midterms. They have taken control of the Senate and the House of Representatives too. Senate The results in the Senate are beyond what the Democrats would have expected. North Carolina was a likely pick-up but the previously deep red state of South Carolina was a huge shock and Kansas had not returned a Democratic senator since 1932. Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Maine also turned blue and the Democrats held Michigan. There are two seats remaining, Alaska and Mississippi, both are on a knife edge. The shift from Republican to Democrat happened across the country. Some of the biggest swings since the presidential election in 2024 were in Texas, where the Democrats took the Senate seat and the governor. Several counties on the state's southern border swung by more than 50 percentage points. House The BBC's partner CBS News projected the Democrats would win the House just after 03:00 GMT on Wednesday (22:00 EST Tuesday). Now it's a question of how big that win will be as counting continues. Two significant seats are Florida 14 and Florida 25 which the Democrats have held. This is a blow to the Republicans' attempt to redraw the boundaries in their favour. The redistricting saw both districts move from having a majority of 2024 Kamala Harris voters to having a majority of people who voted for Donald Trump. Florida 22, which was also redrawn to favour the Republicans, saw a victory for the Democrats too. What turned the vote? A huge poll of voters suggests women turned out in numbers and most voted Democrat. Men on the other hand were evenly split between the two main parties. Hispanic voters look to be one of the key groups in the elections in Texas. The poll suggests this group backed the Democratic Senate candidate James Talerico by 68% to 30% for the Republican Ken Paxton. This is a turnaround from the estimated 50% of Hispanic voters who backed Donald Trump in 2024. The poll also asked what issues voters were most concerned about. It suggests that across the country the economy was the biggest issue, followed by the state of democracy. When voters were asked if Donald Trump's policies impacted economic conditions, the poll suggests that two-thirds believe they had made things worse. Produced by Wesley Stephenson, Christine Jeavans, Daniel Wainwright, Becky Dale, Libby Rogers, Jess Carr, John Walton and Rob England. news.title: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty
news.summary: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says "the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt".
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty
news.summaryTr: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says "the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt".
news.articleText: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty - Published Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says he is retiring from international football. The 41-year-old forward has scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for his country - both world records - since making his debut in 2003. He walked out of the Portugal camp in September after being told he would not start the Nations League match against Denmark, resulting in a £215 fine and a 30-day suspension. "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," Ronaldo said in an Instagram video., external "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world. "Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone - they are also made with the heart. "A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end." On Friday Portugal will announce their squad for this month's Nations League fixtures - against Denmark at home and Wales away. The PFF said it not "let this farewell take place without due tribute". A statement read: "It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo's immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much." Ronaldo played in six European Championships. Portugal were runners-up in 2004 and champions in 2016, but did not progress beyond the semi-finals of the World Cup during his career. Portugal captain since 2008, he won the inaugural Nations League in 2019 and in 2025. Ronaldo's great rival and Argentina legend Lionel Messi retired from international football on an emotional night in front of an 85,000-strong crowd in Buenos Aires in October. Why did Ronaldo fall out with Portugal coach? Ronaldo started every match in his sixth World Cup this summer, when Portugal lost to eventual champions Spain in the last 16. His peformances in the tournament drew criticism in the media, with many observers questioning if he remained a force at international level. He fell out with new coach Jorge Jesus after being named as a substitute against Norway. Ronaldo was reportedly angry at being made to warm up in the second half but not brought on - the first time he was an unused substitute in a competitive Portugal game since 2008. When Jesus said Ronaldo would not start against Denmark, Ronaldo left the camp and issued a lengthy statement in which he said he would not be retiring and that Jesus had twice "broke his word". Jesus said the door remained open for a return, while the PFF fined Ronaldo and suspended him for 30 days - a period that did not include any Portugal games. Ronaldo did not reference the falling-out in his farewell video, but acknowledged that he had made mistakes. "There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember. I made mistakes; I suffered," he said. "There were also moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal. "I spent my life working to become the best player in the world. Today I realise my greatest victory was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world." - Ronaldo's most iconic moments as he retires from international football - Published1 hour ago Rivals: Messi v Ronaldo Watch on BBC iPlayer
