news.title: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown
news.summary: A consultation will consider fines and other ways to clamp down on dangerous e-bike riders.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown
news.summaryTr: A consultation will consider fines and other ways to clamp down on dangerous e-bike riders.
news.articleText: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown - Published People riding drunk or dangerously on e-bikes – and those who jump red lights - could face on-the-spot fines under plans to curb anti-social behaviour. Firms which run shared e-bike schemes will also be expected to manage their fleets better and provide designated parking areas to keep pavements safe. They could also be required to take out insurance so people can claim compensation if they are hit by someone on a shared bike. It's part of a crackdown on what ministers called the "wild west" of e-biking – with a patchwork of rules across the country often leaving the streets unsafe for pedestrians. A consultation launched on Thursday sets out proposed national standards to make journeys safer for everyone and keep pavements clear, particularly for wheelchair users and families with prams. The first e-bikes were launched in Exeter in 2016 and arrived in London a year later, growing to become a popular commuter option. According to the Greater London Authority, 37 million trips were taken on dockless e-bikes last year – a third more than the previous year. Shared e-bikes - such as Lime, Voi, Beryl, Dott, Forest and Bolt - make short journeys quick and convenient. While some areas enforce rules that mean shared bikes can only be left in specific areas, others have looser rules. Under the government's proposals, local leaders will be able to license schemes in their area, allowing them to enforce minimum standards and better integrate e-bikes into existing transport networks. Measures could include requiring operators to have a parking plan and to manage fleet sizes and operating areas, so bikes aren't overcrowding streets. The consultation will also consider ways to tackle antisocial and illegal behaviour, to prevent users from riding shared cycles drunk, underage, or on pavements. There will also be clear consequences set out – such as fines for this type of behaviour. The government is also consulting on whether local leaders should have extra powers, including setting fees and requirements for operators to share data to improve enforcement and journey planning. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the e-bike clampdown was a "small but important everyday fix" which would make streets safer. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said the changes would "stop nuisance parking, tackle antisocial behaviour and make journeys safer". Bosses at Lime, Voi and Bolt all welcomed the proposals, adding that consistent standards being applied across the country would provide clarity and certainty for operators, riders and the general public. news.title: Second buyer makes rescue bid for Poundland as retailer faces collapse
news.summary: A little-known investment group has made a bid to buy the business.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Second buyer makes rescue bid for Poundland as retailer faces collapse
news.summaryTr: A little-known investment group has made a bid to buy the business.
news.articleText: Second buyer makes rescue bid for Poundland as retailer faces collapse - Published A second buyer has made a rescue bid for Poundland as the discount retailer teeters on the brink of collapse, with thousands of jobs at risk. London-based Xyra Group has offered to pay off half of Poundland's outstanding debts - a key sticking point in takeover talks so far - immediately. The rest would be deferred. With Poundland close to collapse, US-based owners Gordon Brothers have already rejected a rival bid from an Irish property group which would have saved its 12,000 staff. Gordon Brothers said the business has faced years of instability and "remains challenged and vulnerable". Sources familiar with the offer said Xyra is offering to immediately pay off £12.5m of an outstanding £30m loan on Poundland's books. The offer came as Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds held crunch talks with Gordon Brothers about the future of the business, urging the investment firm to protect staff however possible. Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, committed at the meeting to prioritise offers which protect its shops and workers. The company said: "We are pursuing all avenues through the sale process to find a solution which protects as many jobs as possible and preserves value. Work continues at pace, engaging in active discussions on offers with interested parties." Xyra is offering to pay off a higher proportion of Poundland's outstanding debts than Martin Property Group, which previously submitted a bid that Gordon Brothers rejected. But doubts remain about the credibility of Xyra's offer, as there is little evidence they meet Gordon Brothers' tests, including whether they have the money and whether they would be good long-term owners of Poundland. Sources pointed to the appointment of Andrew Brode to Xyra's board as a sign of its credibility. Brode works for RWS - a company that provides AI solutions for businesses. Judith MacKenzie, head of Downing Fund Managers, told the BBC Brode is "well known and very credible" among small businesses in the UK. But she said there is "hardly any information" publicly available about Xyra. "So, although some of the people look good, I can't find any evidence to say that they've got the money to back it up yet," MacKenzie added. Gordon Brothers said: "Our intent throughout the comprehensive sale process has been to protect as many jobs as possible and preserve value in order to deliver the best available outcome for all the people, creditors and local communities who care about this business as much as we do." Both Reynolds and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have questioned why a deal for the future of Poundland has not yet been made. Though Xyra made an offer to take over the whole business, it is unclear whether it would keep Poundland together as its owner or break the company up. Several Poundland suppliers have said they would also go bust if the retailer collapses. Its founder Steve Smith said two or three thousand suppliers to the firm, those who solely work for Poundland, would be caught up in the collapse. He added that not only would Poundland's 12,000 staff be affected in that case, but potentially up to 30,000 overall. Related topics - Published2 days ago - Published5 hours ago

news.title: South Korea seeks 4th crypto tax delay, targets 2029 start
news.summary: South Korea is seeking a fourth delay to its 22% crypto tax, months after reaffirming plans to begin taxing digital asset gains in January 2027.

news.titleTr: South Korea seeks 4th crypto tax delay, targets 2029 start
news.summaryTr: South Korea is seeking a fourth delay to its 22% crypto tax, months after reaffirming plans to begin taxing digital asset gains in January 2027.
news.articleText: South Korea seeks 4th crypto tax delay, targets 2029 start South Korea is seeking a fourth delay to its 22% crypto tax, months after reaffirming plans to begin taxing digital asset gains in January 2027. South Korea’s government has backed postponing tax on cryptocurrency gains by another two years to 2029, in what would be the fourth delay to its implementation. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il announced the proposal Thursday, saying the government would consult lawmakers on postponing the January 2027 implementation date. The tax would impose a 22% levy, comprising a 20% income tax and 2% local tax, on annual crypto gains exceeding 2.5 million won ($1,860). The government cited 2029 as the start of information exchange with the US under the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). It said imposing the tax before those exchanges begin could put the domestic market at a disadvantage relative to overseas markets. It also wants to account for changes under planned digital asset legislation. Officials also said they plan to introduce a three-year loss carryforward provision, allowing investors to offset crypto losses against profits earned over the following three years. The government plans to submit amendments to improve the tax system during parliament’s regular session in 2027, with detailed tax guidelines planned for the first half of 2028. The tax was originally scheduled to take effect in January 2022 but was subsequently postponed to 2023, 2025 and 2027. The proposal reverses the government’s previous position. A Finance Ministry official said in May that implementation would proceed in 2027. South Korean finance officials recently engaged with major crypto exchanges amid growing calls to postpone the tax. Industry representatives cited unresolved tax rules for different transaction types and insufficient time to prepare the necessary infrastructure. Related: South Korea plans cybersecurity overhaul after attacks hit banks, crypto firms

news.summary: Easily the most anticipated Bollywood film of the year, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two parts.

news.titleTr: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics
news.summaryTr: Easily the most anticipated Bollywood film of the year, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two parts.
news.articleText: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics - Published India's most expensive film - a lavish retelling of the Hindu epic Ramayana, made in two parts for a reported $500m (£370m) - has opened in cinemas worldwide, sparking enormous expectations and mixed reviews. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two planned films, a sprawling production that brings together some of India's biggest stars, Hollywood visual-effects expertise and two Oscar-winning composers in an attempt to take one of the country's most revered stories to a global audience. One of Hinduism's foundational epics, the Ramayana has travelled across centuries and continents, finding expression in poetry, temple sculpture, shadow puppetry, folk theatre and stories passed down through generations. It has outlasted kingdoms and empires, inspired religious devotion and political movements, and found new life, again and again, on TV and in cinema. Tiwari's version returns to the familiar story of love, duty, exile and war, set in a world of gods and demons, celestial weapons and mighty kingdoms. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Ram, the virtuous prince of Ayodhya. Banished from his kingdom for 14 years, he retreats to the forest with his wife Sita (played by Sai Pallavi), who is kidnapped by Ravana, the 10-headed king of Lanka. Played by Yash, one of southern India's biggest stars, Ravana is a powerful warrior whose pride leads him into an epic battle with Ram (which will be depicted in part 2, set to release next year). The film's producer, Namit Malhotra, heads visual-effects company DNEG, which has worked on Hollywood blockbusters including Dune and Interstellar. The music is a collaboration between AR Rahman, the Oscar-winning Indian composer of Slumdog Millionaire, and Hans Zimmer, whose scores for Gladiator, The Dark Knight and Dune have helped define the sound of modern Hollywood. The film opened days ahead of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights which celebrates Ram's return to Ayodhya after his exile. But the critical response so far has been mixed. Saibal Chatterjee of NDTV channel gave it, external three out of five stars, saying its visual spectacle often overshadowed the story. Its enormous scale, he wrote, "remains, for the most part, the only thing that stands out", while the acting remains "wildly inconsistent". Rishabh Suri of the Hindustan Times newspaper was more enthusiastic, awarding it four stars. "I am happy to report, all that money shows on screen," he wrote, praising the performances and visual effects, though he found the first half sluggish and the music underwhelming. Shubhra Gupta, external of The Indian Express, who gave the film three stars, confessed to initial misgivings about its extravagant scale but found herself gradually won over, calling it the "perfect epic". There was "enough sorcery and thrills and adventure" to sustain the spectacle, she wrote, and the filmmakers had managed to tell a sprawling story without being swallowed by it. Internationally, too, the film drew contrasting reactions. Writing in The Guardian, Peter Bradshaw called it a "thoroughly engaging, rousing and spectacular Indian epic melodrama". He found echoes of Shakespeare in the royal intrigue that sends Rama into exile, and of Homer in his quest to rescue Sita. Its sweeping landscapes and fantastical imagery reminded him of The Lord of the Rings and The Lion King. "It's a rather amazing adventure," he wrote, external, giving it four stars. Others were less impressed. Siddhant Adlakha of IGN scored the film four out of 10, describing its action as "clunky" and its computer-generated imagery as an "eye-sore". Giovanni Lago of Next Best Picture, who gave it, external five out of 10, praised Yash's magnetic Ravana and the score by Rahman and Zimmer. But he felt the film's vast narrative might have been better served by a Game of Thrones-style series. The use of AI to adjust actors' lip movements for the English-language version also drew criticism. While Tiwari said it was intended to make the film more accessible to international audiences, Adlakha likened the result to "exaggerated mouth movements superimposed on still images for comedy sketches". In India, the film has invited comparisons with earlier adaptations, particularly Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan, which captivated the country nearly four decades ago with simple sets and special effects that now seem quaint. When the series first aired in 1987, Sunday mornings across India took on an almost devotional stillness. Streets emptied, shops lowered their shutters and neighbours crowded around TV sets. Some viewers bathed, lit incense and garlanded their screens before the broadcast, preparing for the show much as they might for worship. Arvind Rajagopal, a media scholar at New York University, told the BBC in 2019 that trains and buses would stop and passengers disembark to watch the show on roadside TVs. Broadcast on the state-run Doordarshan network, some of the most popular parts of the 78-episode series drew an estimated 80-100 million viewers, astonishing numbers at a time when owning a TV was a luxury in India. The actors, too, became objects of reverence. Arun Govil, who played Ram, has recalled people weeping at the sight of him and touching his feet. Now, in a casting choice brimming with nostalgia, Govil returns in Tiwari's film as Dasharatha, Ram's father. Other adaptations found their own ways to reimagine the epic. The 1992 Indo-Japanese animated film Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Rama brought the tale to life through richly detailed, hand-drawn animation. Tiwari's Ramayana arrives with technological resources its predecessors could barely have imagined - but also with the expectations of generations who have grown up with the story and its characters. It also comes at a politically charged moment in India, where Ram has become a powerful symbol of Hindu identity - over the past decade and a half, even popular analyses or retellings of the epic have landed in controversy. The 2023 film Adipurush, another big-budget retelling of Ramayana, sparked backlash on several fronts. Hindu groups called for a ban, accusing it of disrespecting religious figures, while some critics questioned its depiction of Ravana, which they said drew on Mughal imagery and reinforced stereotypes about Muslims. The film was also criticised for its dialogue and visual effects. For the actors portraying these characters in the latest film, that burden was deeply felt. "I was filled with fear," Kapoor told the BBC Asian Network's Haroon Rashid. "I knew that maybe I'm too old for this. I won't be able to do justice to it." He called the role "an opportunity of a lifetime", but said playing a figure worshipped by millions left little room for the creative freedom he had enjoyed in other films. Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita, said the experience was as much spiritual as artistic. Raised in a religious household, she said she approached the part not just as a performance, but as an opportunity for personal growth. How the film is being received will become clearer soon, as audiences head to cinemas. But whatever the verdict, it marks a major cultural moment for India, bringing a story loved for generations to the big screen on an unprecedented scale.

news.title: France budget rejection sidelines stablecoin tax, wallet reporting
news.summary: Three adopted amendments, including stablecoin taxation and self-custody reporting, fall away but could be reintroduced in the Senate.

news.titleTr: France budget rejection sidelines stablecoin tax, wallet reporting
news.summaryTr: Three adopted amendments, including stablecoin taxation and self-custody reporting, fall away but could be reintroduced in the Senate.
news.articleText: France budget rejection sidelines stablecoin tax, wallet reporting Three adopted amendments, including stablecoin taxation and self-custody reporting, fall away but could be reintroduced in the Senate. The French National Assembly rejected the 2027 state budget’s revenue section late Wednesday, removing crypto-related amendments from the version of the bill sent to the Senate. The Assembly rejected the revenue section by a vote of 458–0 at first reading, with two abstentions, according to the official voting record. The revenue section covers government income, such as taxes. After the rejection, the government will send the Senate the original budget text, without the crypto-related amendments adopted by lawmakers. The proposals could still be reintroduced in the Senate and would need to survive the remaining budget process to become law. Faustine Fleuret, global head of public affairs at lending protocol Morpho, told Cointelegraph before the vote that rejection of the revenue section could “result in the rejection of the entire bill in the National Assembly, including provisions adopted by way of amendments.” Self-custody reporting and stablecoin tax proposals fall away The Assembly adopted three crypto-related amendments before rejecting the revenue section. On Oct. 16, lawmakers adopted an amendment that would make gains from crypto-to-stablecoin conversions taxable. On Tuesday, lawmakers adopted another amendment that would require taxpayers to disclose self-custodied crypto holdings totaling at least 100,000 euros ($112,000), with the threshold assessed on Dec. 31 of the tax year. Another amendment would increase penalties from 10,000 euros to 50,000 euros for crypto platforms failing to provide information requested by tax authorities. The Senate is scheduled to begin debating the finance bill on Nov. 20, followed by an examination of the revenue section’s articles on Nov. 23, according to its schedule. Related: EU investors rank crypto above retirement plans for lasting wealth creation: OKX survey

news.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
news.summary: Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law.

news.titleTr: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
news.summaryTr: Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law.
news.articleText: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years - Published Joshua Wong, once the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, has been sentenced to 10 years in jail for colluding with foreign forces under the city's sweeping national security law. Wong is among hundreds of campaigners and ordinary Hongkongers arrested under the law, which was imposed in 2020 following explosive pro-democracy protests against Beijing's growing control. Critics say the far-reaching law has silenced dissent, but authorities argue that it is needed to maintain stability and deny it has weakened the city's cherished autonomy. Having already spent the last six years in jail, Wong, who was due to be freed in January, will now spend another decade behind bars. - Silenced and erased, Hong Kong's decade of protest is now a defiant memory - Published30 November 2024 - What a defiant mogul's trial says about Hong Kong - Published18 December 2023 Wong, who turned 30 last month, has already been imprisoned multiple times for his activism which started when he was a teen. On Thursday, he arrived in court wearing a dark blue long-sleeved shirt, khaki trousers and black-rimmed glasses. He looked slimmer compared to his previous public appearances. He nodded in greeting towards members of the packed public gallery, and took notes intermittently as the judge read out the reasons for his sentencing. A crowd had gathered outside the court, with dozens of Hongkongers having queued for hours hoping to get a seat in the public gallery. There was also a heavy police presence. Wong is already serving time for subversion and was due to be freed early next year when he was handed the latest charges, which he has pleaded guilty to earlier in September. Two months and two days of the 10-year term will be served concurrently with his ongoing sentence, the judge said on Thursday. Prosecutors said that Wong had conspired with other campaigners, including self-exiled activist Nathan Law, to lobby for foreign sanctions and blockades against Beijing. These activities took place between July and late November 2020, the court heard. Wong and Law had been co-founders of Demosisto, a now defunct pro-democracy political party. On Thursday, Hong Kong's chief executive John Lee said Wong and Law were "among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong's prosperity and stability". Their actions "not only severely undermined national sovereignty, security, and development interests, but also directly prejudiced the well-being of the general public and the stability of society," Lee said in a statement issued after the ruling. Beijing's foreign ministry said China "firmly supports [Hong Kong] in safeguarding national security in accordance with the law". It also called on "relevant parties" to "earnestly respect China's sovereignty and Hong Kong's legal system". Wong's friend and fellow activist Frances Hui, now based in the US, says she is "heartbroken" and "outraged" by the verdict. "Today's sentencing is not just about Joshua. It is part of a broader political crackdown that seeks to rewrite a chapter of Hong Kong's history and erase the contributions of an entire generation who believed they could shape the future of their city," she told the BBC. Human Rights Watch described the ruling as "cruel and unjust". "To keep Hong Kong society subdued, and to reduce the chance of an international outcry, the Hong Kong government appears to have adopted the tactic of stacking charges against influential pro-democracy leaders," said its Asia director Elaine Pearson. The harshest sentence under the controversial national security law (NSL) thus far has been handed to former media tycoon Jimmy Lai, who was jailed for 20 years, also for colluding with foreign forces. Who is Joshua Wong? Born to IT professional Roger and homemaker Grace in October 1996, Wong was diagnosed with dyslexia as a child, which made him struggle with school. However, he was quick to challenge established rules and norms when they didn't make sense. In secondary school, he rallied with his classmates to protest against the high prices of canteen lunches on Facebook. In 2011, Wong, then 14, co-founded the pro-democracy student activist group Scholarism, which quickly grew in size and influence. The following year, the group rallied more than 100,000 people to protest against Hong Kong's plans to implement mandatory "patriotic education" in schools, forcing the authorities to back down. By 2014, Wong, who was then at the forefront of a civil disobedience movement known as the "Umbrella Movement", had already become one of the most recognisable faces of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement. In 2016, he co-founded Demosisto with Law and Agnes Chow, an activist who is now also in exile. But he often expressed discomfort at being labelled a "protest leader". "We have a lot of facilitators in this movement and I'm one of them... Instead of having a top-down command, we now have a bottom-up command hub," Wong told The Financial Times in November 2019. Demosisto disbanded in 2020, the year Beijing introduced the NSL in Hong Kong. Law left for the UK and continued his advocacy abroad, while Wong stayed on in Hong Kong and tried to run for a seat in its legislature – but was barred, with authorities citing his opposition to the NSL as one of the reasons. Meanwhile, the court cases against Wong were stacking up. On 23 November 2020, he pleaded guilty to several charges related to his involvement in protests outside the Hong Kong police headquarters in 2019. Then came the NSL charges. While still in prison in February 2021, Wong was among 47 people charged with "conspiracy to commit subversion". The group became known as the Hong Kong 47 and remains the largest prosecution so far under the NSL. Wong was still serving his 56-month sentence for the subversion conviction when he was charged with collusion under the NSL last year. On 22 November 2020, the day before he pleaded guilty to the protest charges, Wong wrote in a post on Instagram addressed to "the people of Hong Kong": "To be honest, I have never had much faith in Hong Kong's politics, but I have every confidence in the people of Hong Kong. "Even as political power now poses a comprehensive challenge to the resilience of our civil society, I believe the people of Hong Kong will, as always, find a way to see things through." Wong's friend and fellow activist Frances Hui, now based in the US, says she is "heartbroken" and "outraged" by the verdict. "Today's sentencing is not just about Joshua. It is part of a broader political crackdown that seeks to rewrite a chapter of Hong Kong's history and erase the contributions of an entire generation who believed they could shape the future of their city," she told the BBC. Human Rights Watch described the ruling as "cruel and unjust". "To keep Hong Kong society subdued, and to reduce the chance of an international outcry, the Hong Kong government appears to have adopted the tactic of stacking charges against influential pro-democracy leaders," said its Asia director Elaine Pearson. The harshest sentence under the controversial national security law (NSL) thus far has been handed to former media tycoon Jimmy Lai, who was jailed for 20 years, also for colluding with foreign forces. Who is Joshua Wong? Born to IT professional Roger and homemaker Grace in October 1996, Wong was diagnosed with dyslexia as a child, which made him struggle with school. However, he was quick to challenge established rules and norms when they didn't make sense. In secondary school, he rallied with his classmates to protest against the high prices of canteen lunches on Facebook. In 2011, Wong, then 14, co-founded the pro-democracy student activist group Scholarism, which quickly grew in size and influence. The following year, the group rallied more than 100,000 people to protest against Hong Kong's plans to implement mandatory "patriotic education" in schools, forcing the authorities to back down. By 2014, Wong, who was then at the forefront of a civil disobedience movement known as the "Umbrella Movement", had already become one of the most recognisable faces of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement. In 2016, he co-founded Demosisto with Law and Agnes Chow, an activist who is now also in exile. But he often expressed discomfort at being labelled a "protest leader". "We have a lot of facilitators in this movement and I'm one of them... Instead of having a top-down command, we now have a bottom-up command hub," Wong told The Financial Times in November 2019. Demosisto disbanded in 2020, the year Beijing introduced the NSL in Hong Kong. Law left for the UK and continued his advocacy abroad, while Wong stayed on in Hong Kong and tried to run for a seat in its legislature – but was barred, with authorities citing his opposition to the NSL as one of the reasons. Meanwhile, the court cases against Wong were stacking up. On 23 November 2020, he pleaded guilty to several charges related to his involvement in protests outside the Hong Kong police headquarters in 2019. Then came the NSL charges. While still in prison in February 2021, Wong was among 47 people charged with "conspiracy to commit subversion". The group became known as the Hong Kong 47 and remains the largest prosecution so far under the NSL. Wong was still serving his 56-month sentence for the subversion conviction when he was charged with collusion under the NSL last year. On 22 November 2020, the day before he pleaded guilty to the protest charges, Wong wrote in a post on Instagram addressed to "the people of Hong Kong": "To be honest, I have never had much faith in Hong Kong's politics, but I have every confidence in the people of Hong Kong. "Even as political power now poses a comprehensive challenge to the resilience of our civil society, I believe the people of Hong Kong will, as always, find a way to see things through." news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball
news.articleText: Release Number 9314-26 CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball October 26, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the National Basketball Association today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to protect the integrity of professional basketball in prediction markets. Through the MOU, the CFTC and NBA will better share information by regularly communicating and discussing matters relating to integrity, as well as maintaining fair and transparent prediction markets. “I’m pleased the CFTC and NBA signed an MOU which continues the Commission’s commitment to increasing data sharing between the agency and professional sports leagues,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The NBA joins the MLB and NHL in taking a responsible step toward protecting sports integrity and market participants from abuses in prediction markets like insider trading and fraud. items.articleText: Bankacılık sektörünün mevduatı azaldı, kredi hacmi arttı - Bankacılık sektörünün toplam mevduatı 30 Ekim haftasında geriledi. Sektörün toplam mevduatı 34 trilyon 105 milyar liraya inerken, kredi hacmi 28 trilyon 222,3 milyar liraya yükseldi. - Bankacılık sektörünün toplam kredi hacminin 30 Ekim itibarıyla 29 trilyon lirayı geçtiği bildirildi. Bankacılık sektörünün toplam mevduatı, 30 Ekim ile biten haftada bir önceki haftaya göre 109 milyar 731 milyon 981 bin lira azalışla 34 trilyon 105 milyar 40 milyon 447 bin liraya geriledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB), haftalık para ve banka istatistiklerini açıkladı. Buna göre, bankacılık sektörünün toplam mevduatı 30 Ekim ile biten haftada yüzde 0,32 azalarak 34 trilyon 214 milyar 772 milyon 427 bin liradan 34 trilyon 105 milyar 40 milyon 447 bin liraya indi. Aynı dönemde yurt içi yerleşiklerin bankalardaki Türk lirası cinsi mevduatı yüzde 0,73 azalışla 18 trilyon 821 milyar 273 milyon 181 bin lira, yabancı para (YP) cinsinden mevduatı yüzde 0,12 artışla 11 trilyon 116 milyar 49 milyon 354 bin lira oldu. Bankalarda bulunan toplam YP mevduatı geçen hafta 261 milyar 248 milyon 15 bin dolar düzeyinde gerçekleşirken, bu tutarın 223 milyar 806 milyon 596 bin doları yurt içinde yerleşik kişilerin hesaplarında toplandı. Yurt içi yerleşiklerin toplam YP mevduatında parite etkisinden arındırılmış veriler dikkate alındığında, 30 Ekim itibarıyla 585 milyon 115 bin dolarlık artış görüldü. Yurt içi yerleşiklerin tüketici kredileri arttı Bankacılık sektöründe yurt içi yerleşiklerin tüketici kredileri, geçen hafta yüzde 1,65 artışla 7 trilyon 45 milyar 268 milyon 641 bin liraya yükseldi. Söz konusu kredilerin 851 milyar 747 milyon 604 bin lirası konut, 42 milyar 584 milyon 455 bin lirası taşıt, 2 trilyon 654 milyar 930 milyon 37 bin lirası ihtiyaç kredileri, 3 trilyon 496 milyar 6 milyon 545 bin lirası ise bireysel kredi kartlarından oluştu. Bankacılık sektörünün toplam kredi hacmi de 30 Ekim ile biten haftada 227 milyar 635 milyon 866 bin lira artarak 27 trilyon 994 milyar 642 milyon 833 bin liradan 28 trilyon 222 milyar 278 milyon 699 bin liraya yükseldi. Bankacılık sektörünün kredi hacmi 29 trilyon lirayı aştı Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumunun (BDDK) yayımladığı haftalık bültene göre, bankacılık sektörünün toplam kredi hacmi 30 Ekim itibarıyla 224 milyar 223 milyon lira artarak 28 trilyon 776 milyar 556 milyon liradan 29 trilyon 779 milyon liraya çıktı. Bankacılık sektöründe toplam mevduat ise bankalar arası dahil, geçen hafta 112 milyar 999 milyon lira azalarak 32 trilyon 852 milyar 309 milyon liradan 32 trilyon 739 milyar 311 milyon liraya geriledi. Tüketici kredileri 3 trilyon 557 milyar liraya yükseldi Tüketici kredilerinin tutarı, bu dönemde 32 milyar 405 milyon lira artarak 3 trilyon 556 milyar 940 milyon liraya çıktı. Bu tutarın 852 milyar 509 milyon lirası konut, 42 milyar 729 milyon lirası taşıt ve 2 trilyon 661 milyar 701 milyon lirası ihtiyaç kredilerinden oluştu. Bu dönemde taksitli ticari kredilerin tutarı 1 trilyon 173 milyar 2 milyon lira artarak 5 trilyon 522 milyar 843 milyon lira oldu. Bankaların bireysel kredi kartı alacakları ise 82 milyar 115 milyon lira artışla 3 trilyon 496 milyar 309 milyon lira düzeyinde gerçekleşti. Bireysel kredi kartı alacaklarının 1 trilyon 298 milyar 714 milyon lirasını taksitli, 2 trilyon 197 milyar 595 milyon lirasını taksitsiz borçlar oluşturdu. Yasal öz kaynaklar arttı Bankacılık sektöründe takipteki alacaklar, 30 Ekim itibarıyla önceki haftaya göre 18 milyar 34 milyon lira artışla 983 milyar 118 milyon liraya çıktı. Takipteki alacakların 709 milyar 184 milyon lirasına özel karşılık ayrıldı. Aynı dönemde bankacılık sisteminin yasal öz kaynakları 23 milyar 894 milyon lira artarak 6 trilyon 210 milyar 913 milyon liraya yükseldi.

items.articleText: BIST 100'de yükseliş devam edecek mi? Tuna Çetinkaya 5 sektöre işaret etti Borsa İstanbul'daki yükselişi değerlendiren Kuzey Menkul Değerler Genel Müdürü Tuna Çetinkaya, BIST 100'de 11.500 puanın üzerinde kalıcılığın kritik olduğunu belirtti. Kayıpların telafi edilebileceğini söyleyen Çetinkaya, yatırımcıların dikkatini çekebilecek 5 sektöre işaret etti. Kuzey Menkul Değerler Genel Müdürü Tuna Çetinkaya, CNBC-e'de Şafak Tükle'nin sunduğu Açılış Öncesi programında Borsa İstanbul'daki son yükselişi, BIST 100 endeksinin teknik görünümünü ve yıl sonuna ilişkin beklentilerini değerlendirdi. ABD'deki ara seçimlerin ardından küresel piyasalarda artan risk iştahının Türkiye piyasalarına da olumlu yansıdığını belirten Çetinkaya, Borsa İstanbul'da son günlerde yaşanan yükselişte fon piyasasına ilişkin belirsizliklerin azalmasının etkili olduğunu söyledi. BIST 100 endeksinin 11.500 puan seviyesini yeniden test etmesini değerlendiren Çetinkaya, teknik açıdan bir dönüş sinyali oluşabilmesi için bazı koşulların yerine gelmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Çetinkaya, endeksin haftayı olumlu tamamlamasının ve 11.500 puanın üzerinde destek oluşturmasının önemli olduğunu belirterek bu seviyede kalıcılık sağlanması gerektiğini ifade etti. Borsa İstanbul'da sert fiyat hareketleri yerine daha dengeli bir yükselişe ihtiyaç duyulduğunu dile getiren Çetinkaya, volatilitenin azalmasının yatırımcı güveninin yeniden oluşması açısından önem taşıdığını söyledi. BIST 100'de kayıplar telafi edilebilir BIST 100 endeksinin son bir ayda yaklaşık yüzde 7'ye yakın değer kaybettiğine dikkat çeken Çetinkaya, bu kaybın önümüzdeki birkaç hafta içerisinde telafi edilebileceğini öngördü. Yıl sonuna doğru piyasanın daha olumlu bir görünüm sergileyebileceğini belirten Çetinkaya, son dönemde yaşanan maddi ve psikolojik kayıpların etkisinin zamanla azalabileceğini ifade etti. Çetinkaya, mevcut yükselişi ilk aşamada bir tepki hareketi olarak değerlendirdiğini ancak piyasalardaki iyimserliğin devam etme ihtimalini daha güçlü gördüğünü söyledi. Borsada yeni yükselişin başlangıcı mı? Borsa İstanbul'da yaşanan sert satışların ardından birçok şirketin değerleme açısından cazip seviyelere gerilediğini belirten Çetinkaya, bazı hisselerin defter değerlerinin altında işlem gördüğüne dikkat çekti. Fon piyasasında yaşanan sorunların yalnızca ilgili hisseleri değil, güçlü şirketlerin paylarını da olumsuz etkilediğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, kredilerin geri çağrılması ve likidite sıkışıklığının satış baskısını artırdığını söyledi. Bu süreçte ortaya çıkan fiyatlamaların orta ve uzun vadeli yatırımcılar açısından fırsata dönüşebileceğini belirten Çetinkaya, mevcut toparlanmanın yeni bir yükseliş döneminin başlangıcı olabileceğini ancak bunun için piyasada dengelenmenin sağlanması gerektiğini vurguladı. Bazı hisselerde yüzde 60'a varan kayıplar yaşandı BIST 30, BIST 50 ve BIST 100 kapsamındaki bazı hisselerde zirve seviyelere göre yüzde 40 ila yüzde 60 arasında değer kayıpları yaşandığını belirten Çetinkaya, bu kayıpların tamamının geri alınmasının beklenmemesi gerektiğini söyledi. Güçlü bilançolara sahip bazı şirketlerin kayıplarını daha kısa sürede telafi edebileceğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, yatırımcıların hisse seçiminde daha dikkatli davranması gerektiğine işaret etti. Çetinkaya, özellikle bankacılık, holding, sanayi, iletişim ve perakende sektörlerindeki büyük ve güçlü şirketlerin öne çıkabileceğini belirtti. Borsa İstanbul'da son günlerde yaşanan yükselişin önemli nedenlerinden birinin fon piyasasındaki belirsizliklerin azalması olduğunu belirten Çetinkaya, tasfiye sürecindeki fonlara ait hisselerin borsa dışında satılmasına yönelik gelişmelerin satış baskısını hafiflettiğini söyledi. Piyasada yaşanan sürecin yatırımcılar ve aracı kurumlar üzerinde ciddi etkiler bıraktığını ifade eden Çetinkaya, normalleşmenin başladığına ilişkin işaretler görüldüğünü ancak güvenin yeniden sağlanmasının zaman alacağını vurguladı. Yıl sonu için iyimser beklenti Küresel piyasalardaki olumlu havanın Türkiye açısından da önemli fırsatlar oluşturabileceğini belirten Çetinkaya, özellikle petrol fiyatlarında yaşanabilecek gerilemenin enflasyonla mücadeleyi destekleyebileceğini söyledi. Enerji maliyetlerindeki olası düşüşün Türkiye ekonomisine olumlu yansıyabileceğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, aralık ayında Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasının faiz indirimine gitme ihtimalinin de takip edileceğini belirtti. Borsa İstanbul'daki toparlanmanın devam edebileceğini ancak bunun sağlıklı bir yükselişe dönüşmesi için teknik seviyelerde kalıcılık, azalan oynaklık ve yatırımcı güveninin yeniden güçlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.

Borsa İstanbul'da yaşanan sert satışların ardından birçok şirketin değerleme açısından cazip seviyelere gerilediğini belirten Çetinkaya, bazı hisselerin defter değerlerinin altında işlem gördüğüne dikkat çekti. Fon piyasasında yaşanan sorunların yalnızca ilgili hisseleri değil, güçlü şirketlerin paylarını da olumsuz etkilediğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, kredilerin geri çağrılması ve likidite sıkışıklığının satış baskısını artırdığını söyledi. Bu süreçte ortaya çıkan fiyatlamaların orta ve uzun vadeli yatırımcılar açısından fırsata dönüşebileceğini belirten Çetinkaya, mevcut toparlanmanın yeni bir yükseliş döneminin başlangıcı olabileceğini ancak bunun için piyasada dengelenmenin sağlanması gerektiğini vurguladı. Bazı hisselerde yüzde 60'a varan kayıplar yaşandı BIST 30, BIST 50 ve BIST 100 kapsamındaki bazı hisselerde zirve seviyelere göre yüzde 40 ila yüzde 60 arasında değer kayıpları yaşandığını belirten Çetinkaya, bu kayıpların tamamının geri alınmasının beklenmemesi gerektiğini söyledi. Güçlü bilançolara sahip bazı şirketlerin kayıplarını daha kısa sürede telafi edebileceğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, yatırımcıların hisse seçiminde daha dikkatli davranması gerektiğine işaret etti. Çetinkaya, özellikle bankacılık, holding, sanayi, iletişim ve perakende sektörlerindeki büyük ve güçlü şirketlerin öne çıkabileceğini belirtti. Borsa İstanbul'da son günlerde yaşanan yükselişin önemli nedenlerinden birinin fon piyasasındaki belirsizliklerin azalması olduğunu belirten Çetinkaya, tasfiye sürecindeki fonlara ait hisselerin borsa dışında satılmasına yönelik gelişmelerin satış baskısını hafiflettiğini söyledi. Piyasada yaşanan sürecin yatırımcılar ve aracı kurumlar üzerinde ciddi etkiler bıraktığını ifade eden Çetinkaya, normalleşmenin başladığına ilişkin işaretler görüldüğünü ancak güvenin yeniden sağlanmasının zaman alacağını vurguladı. Yıl sonu için iyimser beklenti Küresel piyasalardaki olumlu havanın Türkiye açısından da önemli fırsatlar oluşturabileceğini belirten Çetinkaya, özellikle petrol fiyatlarında yaşanabilecek gerilemenin enflasyonla mücadeleyi destekleyebileceğini söyledi. Enerji maliyetlerindeki olası düşüşün Türkiye ekonomisine olumlu yansıyabileceğini ifade eden Çetinkaya, aralık ayında Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasının faiz indirimine gitme ihtimalinin de takip edileceğini belirtti. Borsa İstanbul'daki toparlanmanın devam edebileceğini ancak bunun sağlıklı bir yükselişe dönüşmesi için teknik seviyelerde kalıcılık, azalan oynaklık ve yatırımcı güveninin yeniden güçlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.

items.titleTr: How America voted in maps and charts
items.summaryTr: See the maps and charts that show how America voted in the US midterm elections.
items.articleText: How America voted in maps and charts - Published It's been an extraordinary night for the Democrats in the US midterms. They have taken control of the Senate and the House of Representatives too. Senate The results in the Senate are beyond what the Democrats would have expected. North Carolina was a likely pick-up but the previously deep red state of South Carolina was a huge shock and Kansas had not returned a Democratic senator since 1932. Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Maine also turned blue and the Democrats held Michigan. There are two seats remaining, Alaska and Mississippi, both are on a knife edge. The shift from Republican to Democrat happened across the country. Some of the biggest swings since the presidential election in 2024 were in Texas, where the Democrats took the Senate seat and the governor. Several counties on the state's southern border swung by more than 50 percentage points. House The BBC's partner CBS News projected the Democrats would win the House just after 03:00 GMT on Wednesday (22:00 EST Tuesday). Now it's a question of how big that win will be as counting continues. Two significant seats are Florida 14 and Florida 25 which the Democrats have held. This is a blow to the Republicans' attempt to redraw the boundaries in their favour. The redistricting saw both districts move from having a majority of 2024 Kamala Harris voters to having a majority of people who voted for Donald Trump. Florida 22, which was also redrawn to favour the Republicans, saw a victory for the Democrats too. What turned the vote? A huge poll of voters suggests women turned out in numbers and most voted Democrat. Men on the other hand were evenly split between the two main parties. Hispanic voters look to be one of the key groups in the elections in Texas. The poll suggests this group backed the Democratic Senate candidate James Talerico by 68% to 30% for the Republican Ken Paxton. This is a turnaround from the estimated 50% of Hispanic voters who backed Donald Trump in 2024. The poll also asked what issues voters were most concerned about. It suggests that across the country the economy was the biggest issue, followed by the state of democracy. When voters were asked if Donald Trump's policies impacted economic conditions, the poll suggests that two-thirds believe they had made things worse. Produced by Wesley Stephenson, Christine Jeavans, Daniel Wainwright, Becky Dale, Libby Rogers, Jess Carr, John Walton and Rob England. items.title: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty
items.summary: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says "the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt".
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty
items.summaryTr: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says "the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt".
items.articleText: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty - Published Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says he is retiring from international football. The 41-year-old forward has scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for his country - both world records - since making his debut in 2003. He walked out of the Portugal camp in September after being told he would not start the Nations League match against Denmark, resulting in a £215 fine and a 30-day suspension. "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," Ronaldo said in an Instagram video., external "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world. "Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone - they are also made with the heart. "A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end." On Friday Portugal will announce their squad for this month's Nations League fixtures - against Denmark at home and Wales away. The PFF said it not "let this farewell take place without due tribute". A statement read: "It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo's immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much." Ronaldo played in six European Championships. Portugal were runners-up in 2004 and champions in 2016, but did not progress beyond the semi-finals of the World Cup during his career. Portugal captain since 2008, he won the inaugural Nations League in 2019 and in 2025. Ronaldo's great rival and Argentina legend Lionel Messi retired from international football on an emotional night in front of an 85,000-strong crowd in Buenos Aires in October. Why did Ronaldo fall out with Portugal coach? Ronaldo started every match in his sixth World Cup this summer, when Portugal lost to eventual champions Spain in the last 16. His peformances in the tournament drew criticism in the media, with many observers questioning if he remained a force at international level. He fell out with new coach Jorge Jesus after being named as a substitute against Norway. Ronaldo was reportedly angry at being made to warm up in the second half but not brought on - the first time he was an unused substitute in a competitive Portugal game since 2008. When Jesus said Ronaldo would not start against Denmark, Ronaldo left the camp and issued a lengthy statement in which he said he would not be retiring and that Jesus had twice "broke his word". Jesus said the door remained open for a return, while the PFF fined Ronaldo and suspended him for 30 days - a period that did not include any Portugal games. Ronaldo did not reference the falling-out in his farewell video, but acknowledged that he had made mistakes. "There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember. I made mistakes; I suffered," he said. "There were also moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal. "I spent my life working to become the best player in the world. Today I realise my greatest victory was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world." - Ronaldo's most iconic moments as he retires from international football - Published1 hour ago Rivals: Messi v Ronaldo Watch on BBC iPlayer

items.summary: Limak Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ebru Özdemir, Türkiye’nin 2040 enerji hedefleri doğrultusunda yenilenebilir enerji, deniz üstü rüzgar ve nükleer santral yatırımlarında aktif rol almak istediklerini açıkladı. items.titleTr: Ebru Özdemir CNBC-e'ye açıkladı: Limak hangi enerji yatırımlarına hazırlanıyor?
items.summaryTr: Limak Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ebru Özdemir, Türkiye’nin 2040 enerji hedefleri doğrultusunda yenilenebilir enerji, deniz üstü rüzgar ve nükleer santral yatırımlarında aktif rol almak istediklerini açıkladı. Özdemir, enerji ekipmanlarının Türkiye’de üretilmesi konusunda da yatırım fırsatlarını
items.articleText: Ebru Özdemir CNBC-e'ye açıkladı: Limak hangi enerji yatırımlarına hazırlanıyor? - Limak Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ebru Özdemir, Türkiye’nin 2040 enerji hedefleri doğrultusunda yenilenebilir enerji, deniz üstü rüzgar ve nükleer santral yatırımlarında aktif rol almak istediklerini açıkladı. - Özdemir, enerji ekipmanlarının Türkiye’de üretilmesi konusunda da yatırım fırsatlarını değerlendirebileceklerini söyledi. Limak Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ebru Özdemir, CNBC-e canlı yayınında Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanı Alparslan Bayraktar tarafından açıklanan 2040 enerji vizyonunu değerlendiren Özdemir, Türkiye'nin önümüzdeki dönemde elektrik üretim kapasitesini önemli ölçüde artırması gerektiğini söyledi. Limak enerji yatırımlarını artıracak Türkiye'nin 2040 yılına kadar enerji ihtiyacını kendi kaynaklarıyla karşılayabilecek bir yapıya ulaşmasının hedeflendiğini belirten Özdemir, bu süreçte özel sektörün de önemli sorumluluk üstleneceğini ifade etti. Limak Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ebru Özdemir, Limak'ın enerji yatırımlarına ilişkin yol haritasını da paylaştı. Şirketin mevcut hidroelektrik santrallerinin yanı sıra yapımı devam eden iki HES projesi bulunduğunu belirten Özdemir, güneş enerjisinde de büyümeyi hedeflediklerini söyledi. Deniz üstü rüzgar ve nükleer enerjiye ilgi Türkiye’de gündeme gelen deniz üstü rüzgar enerjisi projelerine de değinen Özdemir, bu alanda yabancı şirketlerle görüşmeler yürüttüklerini ve aktif olmak istediklerini açıkladı. Nükleer enerjinin Türkiye’nin elektrik üretim kapasitesindeki artışta önemli rol oynayacağını belirten Özdemir, Sinop ve İğneada'da planlanan santral projelerini yakından takip ettiklerini söyledi. Küçük modüler reaktörler (SMR) alanında da bir ekiplerinin çalıştığını kaydetti. Özdemir, Limak olarak 2040 enerji hedeflerine katkı sağlayacak üretim projelerinde yer almaya devam edeceklerini vurguladı. Enerji ekipmanlarının Türkiye'de üretilmesi de gündemde Özdemir, enerji yatırımlarının yalnızca elektrik üretim kapasitesinin artırılmasıyla sınırlı kalmaması gerektiğine dikkat çekti. Yeni enerji tesislerinde kullanılacak ekipmanların Türkiye'de üretilmesinin önemine işaret eden Özdemir, bu alanda da yatırım fırsatlarının değerlendirilebileceğini belirtti. Türk mühendislerin ve çalışanların üretim süreçlerinde daha fazla yer almasının sanayileşme açısından kritik olduğunu ifade eden Özdemir, Limak'ın imalat tarafında da rol üstlenebileceğinin sinyalini verdi. Türkiye'nin 2040 enerji vizyonunda yenilenebilir kaynakların yanı sıra nükleer enerji ve yeni nesil küçük modüler reaktörler de öne çıkıyor. Deniz üstü rüzgar santralleri ise Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji kapasitesini artırması beklenen yeni yatırım alanları arasında yer alıyor. Limak'ın açıklamaları, şirketin enerji üretiminin yanı sıra enerji ekipmanları imalatına da yönelebileceğine işaret ediyor.

items.title: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
items.summary: Most analysts expected the increase from 3.75% to 4%.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
items.summaryTr: Most analysts expected the increase from 3.75% to 4%.
items.articleText: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years - Published The Bank of England has raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years and signalled a further increase is likely in the coming months unless the US-Iran war is resolved. Rates rose to 4% from 3.75% in a bid to curb inflation mainly driven by the conflict's impact on oil prices. Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, said the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but warned "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase". The higher level will increase the cost of borrowing for things such as mortgages, loans and credit cards, but will also lead to higher returns on savings. The Bank's rate-setting committee all backed increasing interest rates, with eight out of nine policymakers voting in favour of the 0.25pp rise. One member wanted an even bigger increase. Bailey said the rate hike was warranted due to higher energy prices, but stressed it is not the start of a cycle of rate rises. However, the governor pointed to what happens in the Middle East as the main factor in future decisions. "Put simply, it requires real progress towards settling the conflict in the Middle East," he said. Bailey said he could "see the argument" for a further rate hike, before taking a "more conditional approach, dependent on the evidence on energy prices and inflation dynamics". However, members of the rate-setting committee offered different views on the path forward. Clare Lombardelli agreed there was "likely to be a case for a further increase in rates in the near term", but Megan Greene said any decision would depend on how inflation impacts wages, prices and the jobs market. Alan Taylor said the rate rise was a "a risk-management 'one-for-now' insurance hike". The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) measure of inflation is well below its peak of a few years ago but has been heading back up and is expected to go higher. It was 3.5% in the year to September 2026, up from 3.1% the previous month and well above the central bank's 2% target. The ongoing impact of the Iran war, primarily on the cost of energy and fuel, has filtered through to the UK inflation rate. Millions of domestic energy customers are braced for a hefty rise in prices in January. The Bank said in its central forecast it expected inflation to peak at 4.9% in the middle of next year, higher than it originally estimated, and not return to its target of 2% until 2028. In what it called an "adverse scenario", where the US-Iran war could escalate further and send oil and gas prices much higher, inflation could reach 6.2% in 2027, it suggested. While the UK cannot control global energy prices, the Bank is raising rates in order to limit the knock-on effects of high energy prices resulting in inflation going up across the board. The Bank of England last raised rates in August 2023. Its base rate is what it charges other banks and building societies to borrow money, which influences what they charge their own customers for mortgages as well as the interest rate they pay on savings. Higher fuel prices can lead to businesses passing on higher costs to customers. But policymakers said to date there was "limited evidence" this had happened for goods, such as food, with some firms absorbing cost increases and accepting lower margins. The last time the Bank raised interest rates was in August 2023. After a period of rate rises, it began lowering them and had kept them on hold at 3.75% since December last year until now. Its base rate influences the rates High Street banks and other lenders charge on mortgages, loans and credit cards, as well as the interest they pay on savings. The hike on Thursday will see 510,000 tracker mortgage-holders see a £31 monthly jump in repayments, according to banking trade body UK Finance. Homeowners on fixed deals will see no change, though future products may be affected. How people on variable deals will be impacted depending on how their lender reacts. Typically a 0.25pp rise means a £14 increase per month in repayments. The Bank said mortgage approvals for houses had fallen by 8% in the three months to September relative to the three months prior, which was likely down to borrowing costs rising to buy homes since the US-Iran war began. Central banks try to limit price rises by putting up interest rates. The theory is by pushing up the cost of borrowing for things such as mortgages and credit cards, consumers cut back and price rises slow. Higher rates also give people more incentives to save instead of spending. But it's a balancing act as higher rates can also lead to businesses holding off investing and hiring, which can harm the overall economy. - Three ways the interest rate rise could affect you - Published30 minutes ago As of 4 November, the average two-year fixed residential mortgage rate was 5.96%, while the average five-year rate stood at 5.99%, according to financial information service Moneyfacts. It means anyone rolling off a five-year deal faces a much bigger mortgage bill. Broker L&C said average mortgage rates offered by the 10 biggest lenders suggested some borrowers now faced paying almost £5,000 more each year in repayments on a £200,000 mortgage over 25 years than those who secured a remortgage deal in 2021. Five years ago, the average five-year fixed remortgage rate among the 10 biggest lenders was 1.30%. Get in touch Do you have a mortgage, a credit card, a car finance agreement? How are interest rates affecting you? - Published6 days ago

items.articleText: WhatsApp hesabınız ele geçirilirse ne yapmalısınız? Uzmandan 6 kritik uyarı YAYIN TARİHİ, 05 Kasım 2026 15:11 PAYLAŞ - Tüketici Hak Arama Derneği Hukuk İşleri Başkanı Avukat Mehmet Raşit Çavuşoğlu, ele geçirilen WhatsApp hesapları üzerinden yakınlardan para istenebildiğine dikkat çekerek kullanıcıları uyardı. Çavuşoğlu, iki adımlı doğrulamanın etkinleştirilmesini, güvenlik kodlarının paylaşılmamasını ve para taleplerinin farklı bir kanaldan teyit edilmesini önerdi. Tüketici Hak Arama Derneği Hukuk İşleri Başkanı Avukat Mehmet Raşit Çavuşoğlu, artan WhatsApp hesaplarının ele geçirilmesine karşı çeşitli uyarılarda bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Çavuşoğlu, WhatsApp hesap güvenliği ihlallerinin maddiyatı, özel hayatı, haberleşme gizliliğini ve kişisel verileri de etkileyebildiğini belirtti. WhatsApp üzerinden gelen para taleplerinde dikkatli olunması gerektiğini belirten Çavuşoğlu, "Acele ettiren ve farklı bir hesaba para göndermenizi isteyen mesajlarda, ilgili kişiyi bildiğiniz numarasından ayrıca arayıp talebi doğrulayın" dedi. Çavuşoğlu, işletim sistemi ve uygulama güncellemelerinin ertelenmemesi gerektiğini anlatarak, şöyle devam etti: "Uçtan uca şifreleme, mesajların iletim sırasında korunması açısından önemli bir güvenlik katmanıdır. Ancak telefonun veya hesap erişiminin ele geçirilmesine karşı tek başına mutlak güvence sağlamaz. Bir kişinin hesabından onun kimliğine bürünerek yakınlarını aldatıp para göndermelerini sağlamanın, şartları oluştuğunda Türk Ceza Kanunu'nun bilişim sistemlerinin araç olarak kullanılması suretiyle nitelikli dolandırıcılık suçunu oluşturur. Bu suçta, kanuni yaptırım ve indirimler uygulanmadan önceki hapis cezası aralığı 4 yıldan 10 yıla kadardır. Ayrıca 5 bin güne kadar adli para cezası öngörülür. Kanun, para cezasının miktarı bakımından suçtan elde edilen menfaatin 2 katını alt sınır olarak belirler. Her dosyada sonuç ceza, kişinin eylemi ve uygulanacak hükümlere göre mahkemece belirlenir." Çavuşoğlu, konuya ilişkin alınabilecek önlemleri şu şekilde açıkladı: "Telefonun işletim sistemini ve WhatsApp'ı güncel tutun, 2 adımlı doğrulamayı etkinleştirin, doğrulama kodlarınızı ve hesap güvenliği bilgilerinizi kimseyle paylaşmayın. Bağlı cihazlar bölümünü kontrol ederek tanımadığınız oturumlardan çıkış yapın. Bazı gelişmiş saldırılarda yetkisiz erişimin bu listede görünmeyebileceğini unutmayın. Kaynağı belirsiz bağlantıları ve reklamları açmayın, güvenilir olmayan yerlerden uygulama veya dosya indirmeyin. Para talebi tanıdığınız kişinin hesabından gelse bile, transferden önce o kişiye ayrı bir kanaldan ulaşarak doğrulayın."

items.title: Three ways the interest rate rise could affect you
items.summary: Job, loans and savings are all affected by the rise in interest rates announced by the Bank of England.
